Hello, we are Pete and Jon! We think you'll love our place: It's a great, stylish, safe, comfortable, and clean apartment. We strive to create a comfortable environment where you can feel at home and escape from the Mission's busy streets. 

We LOVE this place, and we hope you do too!

Guest Access

You are welcome to use the kitchen and to keep food in the refrigerator and freezer if needed. We have a drip coffee maker for your use, electric tea kettle, toaster oven, microwave, gas range and oven. 

We provide high-speed wireless internet access at no additional charge. WiFi password should be unlocked w/in Airbnb site, but it can also be found on the fridge. 


Interaction with Guests

We go with the flow, but usually our schedules are busy working,  when we can we're out exploring the Mission or Bay Area.  Other times, we'll all hang out in the evening or weekend. When things work out, we've all gone out for dinner, a night on the town, or a walk to the Farmers' market on the weekend.

The Neighborhood

Everything is easily accessible: restaurants, museums, waterfront, shopping -- plus so much more this amazing city has to offer. We're just a short walk to the Castro, Noe Valley, Bernal Heights, and all the nightlife of SoMa -- and just a 2 minute walk from BART. We're near enough of everything that it's easy to get around!

San Francisco has some of the best food in the world, and we've got plenty of places to grab breakfast, lunch or dinner within just a block or two. Let us give you a recommendation to suit your tastes, or explore our local favorites.

Getting Around

We're only minutes walk from Muni, BART, and we're easily freeway-accessible if you're driving. (Parking is challenging so public transport is the way to go!) Uber and taxis are also an easy option. We have a parking space that is sometimes available- ask if needed. 

Other Things to Note
-Our apartment is usually pretty quiet, some street noise, but nothing too heavy.

space: The Pavilion: A San Francisco Tiny House was completed in 2009.   Tiny house living is not for everyone but the Pavilion will give you a chance to try it out.  You'll find recycled and repurposed materials throughout the property, beginning with the custom gate, covering the walls of the fence and even inside on the dining/work table and wood steps.  Architect David Winslow designed the space and Shirley Watts, artist and landscape designer, installed the garden and fence.  The Pavilion has attracted architecture and garden tours from groups around the world and has been a frequent destination for many visiting architecture students.  A rehabbed 1906 earthquake cottage, original to the property, sits adjacent but separate to the Pavilion, linked by an outdoor deck.  A full time tenant-couple share the gate and accesses the cottage via the cobblestone path along the south side of the Pavilion. Please respect their privacy,  as they will honor yours.

The top of Bernal Hill boasts hiking paths and the best views in San Francisco. The nearby strip of Mission Street (right where Mission meets Valencia) is packed with great restaurants (Emmy's Spaghetti is a favorite), cool dive bars, cute cafes and a grocery store. Nearby Precita Park, just down a cute hidden staircase around the block, is also a perfect spot for picnics. In a city known for its freezing cold fog, Bernal Heights happily sits on the sunnier side of the city so you can always expect it to be a few degrees warmer over here. We have great food and great fun on all sides! The rhythm of the Beat poets flow in the streets outside their regular hangouts, like Vesuvio, and City Lights Bookstore, just a couple of blocks away. And we are only a 20 minute walk from the famous Fisherman’s Wharf.

host_about:
There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. At first glance, one might presume that the endgame of all hostels is to create a sense of firm familiarity among guest and staff alike, but with us, you can feel it. With a full roster of events that are ongoing, all inclusive in both experience and price, and a design purposefully conducive to the gathering of folks all around the world, we are dedicated to establishing a world reaching community that you feel while you are here, and long after your stay.

Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

History: The building was built in 1917 and I completely redesigned and remodeled it in 2016 including an earthquake retrofit.  It operates to near-net-zero energy with solar PV panels and solar hot water panels on the roof, and there is some cool energy monitoring and lighting automation to play with or just enjoy.

I'm a Michigander originally, now loving life out here by the beach where the surf is pretty good and never crowded, and my dog is always at least as happy as me/I.  I spent many years in Alaska as an architect, builder, fisherman and float plane pilot, and I lived on my sailboat out of Berkeley and traveled by moto for sailing, mountaineering or rock climbing trips for many years before that (South America rocks).  I think I really found my home in the Outer Sunset, where it all seems to come together.

I suppose at this point I'm a bit of a San Francisco cliche:  I'm a happy bachelor  surfer, architect and builder, self-employed software developer and experimenting with a tech startup that will of course be totally disruptive! (ie really good).  Until recently I worked at Autodesk on energy analysis software, and before that split my time between SF and Alaska on various things from design to consulting to fishing and climbing (it really is the frontier!).

I'm living and working at home much of the time, between as much surfing or biking or walking the dog as I can get.   I'm also always tinkering and finishing up details on the house, working on my moto, or experimenting with electronic gizmos and energy automation.  I just finished rebuilding my old Ford Renger engine (it runs!), and the next project is to build the new shelving system for the giant book wall on the main floor of the house.

The neighborhood is a patchwork of warehouses, swanky nightspots, residential hotels, art spaces, loft apartments, furniture showrooms and the tenacious Internet companies that survived the tech market collapse. Although a lot of building has gone on in recent years, it is still not densely developed. You can walk several desolate blocks before suddenly finding a hopping restaurant. Most of the action can be found in four general areas: by South Park and the Giants ballpark, Moscone, around the SF MOMA and Yerba Buena gardens, and over by Folsom and Eleventh Street. SoMa, as it's known, sounds a little like a SoHo wannabe, and it does have a strong downtown vibe. neighborhood_overview: Our location can't be beat! We are located one block over from the famous San Francisco Chinatown, one block from the bustling Financial District, a few blocks south of "Little Italy" in North Beach, and just a 10 minute stroll from the water along the Embarcadero.

transit: Public transportation is plentiful and nearby, though many things are walking distance. Cars are not recommended since we are right in downtown SF and parking garages are very expensive (about $30/24 hours). There is minimal street parking in front of the hostel: 7pm-7am during the week, and limited on the weekends. Alternatively, we know of some first come, first served free street parking across the city. You can then take a 25 minute bus ride back.
access: Guests have 24/7 access to their dorm, the shared bathrooms, the kitchen, and the common area. Please no cooking between midnight and 6am.
interaction: Reception is available to answer any and all questions between 8am and midnight. Reception is closed from midnight to 8am, though there is always some on site in case of emergency.
house_rules: Check in is available from 8am-midnight each day.  Check out must be by 11am, the day of departure. As a travelers house, all guests are required to have a government issued photo ID and proof of traveling status (i.e. plane tickets or passport). You will be asked for a $20 refundable security deposit at check-in. Most of our rules are common sense and will be explained at check-in. In general, we simply ask that guests follow the golden rule of living in community: "Be Excellent to One Another". If you have any questions, please message me.

Greetings!
Thank you for viewing my profile! We are self employed and also philanthropists residing in San Francisco. My husband and I are high school sweet hearts with four wonderful children!   We love traveling and think of NYC as our second city, being that we visit at least 3 - 4 times a year for 20 years.

Exploring the world to learn about other people and cultures is our passion. We enjoy meeting new friends globally !  When we are at home we love entertaining others, getting together with family, spearheading or volunteering  a community service endeavor, going out to dance for exercise, or attending the local performing arts and theaters.

Mark Twain

Sharon

host_about:
ABOUT ME

I grew up in Cleveland, Ohio and became an exchange student at the age of 16. Living abroad for one year in South Africa changed my life forever. I since went back to live in South Africa a second time. I have had the good fortune of traveling abroad and meeting amazing people along the way. I met a woman on a train who invited me to visit her in Paris. When I got there, she gave me the keys to her apartment and said I could stay as long as I like. From that moment on I made a vow to help as many travelers as possible on their journeys. That is why Air BNB appeals to me; the art of travel, connection, culture, and sharing the City I love so very much with others.

INTERESTS

Spiritual pursuits. Traditional Japanese culture. Tea. Gardening. Reading/listening to books. Taking care of my backyard wildlife. Exploring San Francisco. Cooking, when I have the time to enjoy it. I am passionate about Languages and learning. I am fluent in English, learning Spanish and Japanese, and previously studied Indo-Malay. I am enthusiastic about collecting words and phrases in other languages. I am passionate about animals and nature.

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS

I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R & B, Motown, Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.

Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.

I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,"The Glass Castle,"Your Brain at Work." I listen to Audio Books constantly which is why I get through so many books.

COUNTRIES I’VE VISITED

Japan, Peru, South Africa, Malaysia, Thailand, Switzerland, France, Belgium, Italy

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING

I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take a cruise. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general, I like to keep things simple. 

As a Host, however, I enjoy nurturing Guests and making sure they feel well cared for and even spoiled. My Guests enjoy my many versions of “tea” and also wicked bowls of popcorn! 

I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and desire to make even the ordinary feel special. 

From the lovely view, peaceful setting, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill requests, you can count on having a positive stay and look forward to a return visit to our beloved house on the hill in exciting San Francisco.

neighborhood_overview: The Bayview has until recently, been the best-kept (and sunniest) secret of San Francisco. We are in the very southeast corner of the city, an area that is rapidly transforming with new residential developments. All kinds of little gems are flourishing in our neighborhood as the rest of the city catches on to the great potential of this side of town. Flora Grubb Nursery and Cafe, San Francisco Mead Company, and Old School Cafe are a few local businesses I'd recommend checking out. Our street has a tight-knit community of families who are very active in local affairs.

neighborhood_overview: Bernal Heights frequently tops lists of the most charming neighborhoods in San Francisco, which isn’t surprising given its accessibility, versatility and vibe. Located close to the freeway, this rental property is ideal for those popping into town for a quick business trip or travelers who want to unpack and get to know the city a bit more intimately. The neighborhood is very walkable, and you’ll have easy access to beautiful, pet-friendly parks – two of which are just two blocks away. We also have two awesome local corner stores, one of which specializes in delicious organic produce. San Francisco’s Mission District, one of the most vibrant and colorful parts of San Francisco day or night, is also located nearby. Don't forget to check out 24th street (a few blocks walk north) or Cortland (same distance south).

Prices are firm - all booking inquiries requesting a different price than the one listed will be respectfully declined. We also are happy to offer flexible check-in and check-out times. We know how unpredictable and stressful travel can be. If you are going to arrive early or late, keep us in the loop and we will do our best to accommodate. Unlike many parts of San Francisco, street parking in the Bernal Heights neighborhood is easy (while things still get busy at times, parking is available more often than not), and the nearby BART stop means visitors never have to battle city center traffic and parking when checking out the rest of the city. When you’re ready to explore the city (or greater Bay Area) beyond Bernal Heights, the BART (the Bay Area’s local subway system) is just a 15-minute (1km or .6 mile) walk away, and buses run regularly. If you're a cyclist, that's an option as well - we have a neighborhood bike shop located less than a mile away. If you'd like to travel outside the city but you didn't rent a car, the city has plenty of car sharing options including Getaround, RelayRides, City CarShare and Zipcar - all are easy to use, although you should sign up for an account before arriving to speed up the process.

Wifi, Cable television and Netflix are available for your use as well. There are two full communal bathrooms - both have rainfall style showers. One bathroom is right outside your door, but the other bathroom is also available to you. Each bathroom is stacked with tons of amenities: toothpaste, cotton swabs, toothbrushes, body/hair/hand soaps, and cleaned daily!

neighborhood_overview: The Outer Sunset is one of SFs best kept secrets.  We have slightly cooler weather than downtown, the Mission and the East Bay, but contrary to its reputation as a fog-bound zone, we see sunny days the majority of the time, with an amazing fall period for sunny beach days, great winter surfing, and dry summers.   We are far enough from the hustle and noise of downtown, but only 35 minutes from downtown SF.  It's a mellow version of all the amenities of a city, but without all the crazy hassles with parking, noise and stress. Only a few blocks from Ocean Beach and GG park, this is one of the greatest neighborhoods in SF. Within a couple blocks there is plenty of good eateries and stores on Judah.  Outerlands at 45th is the snazzy place, Beachside at 47th is great creative eggs etc and the best coffee, Sea Breeze between 44th and 45th is the diner-ey spot with something extra, and there's a great vegan place at 44th that surprisingly tastey.  And there's always the amazing cinnamon and s
notes: Cancellations: AirBnB's 'moderate' policy is more strict than I really want, but is closest to what I actually do with manual refunds. I've generally been able to do a full refund for cancellations, as the space re-books pretty quickly.  If you know that you can't make it, please cancel as soon as you can to give time for new bookings.  I will never cancel from my end. History: The building was built in 1917 and I completely redesigned and remodeled it in 2016 including an earthquake retrofit.  It operates to near-net-zero energy with solar PV panels and solar hot water panels on the roof, and there is some cool energy monitoring and lighting automation to play with or just enjoy.
transit: The house is a half-block from N Judah (35 mins downtown, or 20-25 by the express bus, and 15 mins to museums).  It costs about $20 for Uber/Lyft from the airport (choose 'Uber Pool' or 'Lyft Line', it's cheaper and still very fast). Very easy access to South Bay or beach cities on the beautiful Hwy 280 or Hwy 1, and also easy to get to the Marina District, Presidio and the GG bridge and North Bay via GG Park and 19th. East Bay is about 45-60 mins by N-Judah and BART. The house is a half block from a really cool strip of restaurants and shops and things, so it's a great place to be on foot.  There are a couple of bike shops to rent bikes to tour the park or ride across the GG Bridge.  The MUNI tracks also run on Judah Street, making it easy to get to other locales.  The street itself (44th Ave) is very quiet and neighborly, and close enough to the beach and park that I get there twice a day with my dog.  I love living here!
access: Kitchen and bathroom are shared.   Feel free to cook or make coffee and use the fridge and dining table.  Plenty of storage and a nice walk-in closet and coat closet.  The living room is where Desmo and I hang out most of the time, and you're welcome to join us, or you may prefer to hang out in the privacy of the room with wifi, TV, work desk, and a couple comfy chairs.
interaction: As much or as little as you like.   Feel free to have a private stay or some conversations and meals with me.  Let me know in your intro message if you want your stay to be private or social.   The room has TV, internet, desk, chairs and a small table.  The main living area and bathroom are shared with me and my pooch.  The bedroom is a decent size for hanging out, and the kitchen is always available for cooking.   It's generally pretty quiet around here, with random friend visits and some social events.   If you like, I'm glad to share my knowledge of 28 years in SF  and AK and what I love about Ocean Beach.  Speaking for Desmo, she will sit and engage you in conversation any time. Check out my profile page to see what my day to day is like, and feel free to intersect where it interests you.  Dog walks and eating are always good times to meet.
house_rules: Shoes off in the entry for upstairs, please, but shoes on is OK downstairs. If you can't find parking easily, feel free to park in the driveway for a few hours until things open up.  Leave space for the sidewalk.
host_about:
I'm a Michigander originally, now loving life out here by the beach where the surf is pretty good and never crowded, and my dog is always at least as happy as me/I.  I spent many years in Alaska as an architect, builder, fisherman and float plane pilot, and I lived on my sailboat out of Berkeley and traveled by moto for sailing, mountaineering or rock climbing trips for many years before that (South America rocks).  I think I really found my home in the Outer Sunset, where it all seems to come together.

I suppose at this point I'm a bit of a San Francisco cliche:  I'm a happy bachelor  surfer, architect and builder, self-employed software developer and experimenting with a tech startup that will of course be totally disruptive! (ie really good).  Until recently I worked at Autodesk on energy analysis software, and before that split my time between SF and Alaska on various things from design to consulting to fishing and climbing (it really is the frontier!).

I'm living and working at home much of the time, between as much surfing or biking or walking the dog as I can get.   I'm also always tinkering and finishing up details on the house, working on my moto, or experimenting with electronic gizmos and energy automation.  I just finished rebuilding my old Ford Renger engine (it runs!), and the next project is to build the new shelving system for the giant book wall on the main floor of the house.

host_about:
Hello, we are Pete and Jon! We think you'll love our place: It's a great, stylish, safe, comfortable, and clean apartment. We strive to create a comfortable environment where you can feel at home and escape from the Mission's busy streets. 

We LOVE this place, and we hope you do too!

Guest Access

You are welcome to use the kitchen and to keep food in the refrigerator and freezer if needed. We have a drip coffee maker for your use, electric tea kettle, toaster oven, microwave, gas range and oven. 

We provide high-speed wireless internet access at no additional charge. WiFi password should be unlocked w/in Airbnb site, but it can also be found on the fridge. 


Interaction with Guests

We go with the flow, but usually our schedules are busy working,  when we can we're out exploring the Mission or Bay Area.  Other times, we'll all hang out in the evening or weekend. When things work out, we've all gone out for dinner, a night on the town, or a walk to the Farmers' market on the weekend.

The Neighborhood

Everything is easily accessible: restaurants, museums, waterfront, shopping -- plus so much more this amazing city has to offer. We're just a short walk to the Castro, Noe Valley, Bernal Heights, and all the nightlife of SoMa -- and just a 2 minute walk from BART. We're near enough of everything that it's easy to get around!

San Francisco has some of the best food in the world, and we've got plenty of places to grab breakfast, lunch or dinner within just a block or two. Let us give you a recommendation to suit your tastes, or explore our local favorites.

Getting Around

We're only minutes walk from Muni, BART, and we're easily freeway-accessible if you're driving. (Parking is challenging so public transport is the way to go!) Uber and taxis are also an easy option. We have a parking space that is sometimes available- ask if needed. 

Other Things to Note
-Our apartment is usually pretty quiet, some street noise, but nothing too heavy.

host_about:
Hello, we are Pete and Jon! We think you'll love our place: It's a great, stylish, safe, comfortable, and clean apartment. We strive to create a comfortable environment where you can feel at home and escape from the Mission's busy streets. 

We LOVE this place, and we hope you do too!

Guest Access

You are welcome to use the kitchen and to keep food in the refrigerator and freezer if needed. We have a drip coffee maker for your use, electric tea kettle, toaster oven, microwave, gas range and oven. 

We provide high-speed wireless internet access at no additional charge. WiFi password should be unlocked w/in Airbnb site, but it can also be found on the fridge. 


Interaction with Guests

We go with the flow, but usually our schedules are busy working,  when we can we're out exploring the Mission or Bay Area.  Other times, we'll all hang out in the evening or weekend. When things work out, we've all gone out for dinner, a night on the town, or a walk to the Farmers' market on the weekend.

The Neighborhood

Everything is easily accessible: restaurants, museums, waterfront, shopping -- plus so much more this amazing city has to offer. We're just a short walk to the Castro, Noe Valley, Bernal Heights, and all the nightlife of SoMa -- and just a 2 minute walk from BART. We're near enough of everything that it's easy to get around!

San Francisco has some of the best food in the world, and we've got plenty of places to grab breakfast, lunch or dinner within just a block or two. Let us give you a recommendation to suit your tastes, or explore our local favorites.

Getting Around

We're only minutes walk from Muni, BART, and we're easily freeway-accessible if you're driving. (Parking is challenging so public transport is the way to go!) Uber and taxis are also an easy option. We have a parking space that is sometimes available- ask if needed. 

Other Things to Note
-Our apartment is usually pretty quiet, some street noise, but nothing too heavy.

access: Everything other than our bedroom/bathroom is yours to roam!
interaction: Whatever you prefer! We love our city and would be so happy to guide you toward our favorite places, but we’re totally happy to let you do your own thing too.
house_rules: - Note that we have a little dog named Wally. He's well-trained and has a sweet and loving temperament. You can let him roam while you're home if you'd like, but be sure to put him back in that area (and make sure the dining room doors are closed!) before you leave. - Your bedroom is adjacent to ours, and the walls are somewhat thin throughout the apartment, so we ask that you avoid excessive noise between 10pm-6am. neighborhood_overview: Bayview is the sunniest neighborhood in San Francisco and is a short 20-minute MUNI train ride from downtown, AT&T park, the Embarcadero, and other famous SF sights.  Within walking distance of the apartment, you'll find an amazing mix of delicious soul food restaurants, a permanent pizza food truck situated in a succulent garden, hipster coffee shops, a local wine tasting room and a couple of breweries.  Unlike many other parts of the city, Bayview is a long-time home for many SF locals who own their homes and are raising a family in the city. This contributes to the strong sense of community and friendliness that is unique to Bayview, which is a source of pride for us.  Being a traditionally lower-income area that's currently up-and-coming, however, there is a bit of grittiness to our neighborhood. host_about: I first came to San Francisco in 2011 after years of traveling the world (mostly with Airbnb!) I fell in love with the city, and in 2018 became a home-owner and began hosting as a way to re-connect with the nomadic community. As both a host and a guest, I enjoy sharing stories and local tips with those I meet. Having lived in 9 countries and traveled to many more, I strive to be the sort of guest that can fit in anywhere and the sort of host that can make anyone feel at home. During my travels, I studied foreign languages extensively, and though I'm quite rusty these days I always enjoy getting the chance to practice. These days, I get a lot of pleasure from constructing creative integrations between technology and design -- both in my home and in my handmade converted camper-van (#VanLife). When I'm not working, I travel around in the van with my dog, a mini Australian Shepherd named Azuli.

neighborhood_overview: Our Central Richmond Neighborhood incorporates the best of the City.  Our quiet tree-lined street is family oriented and close knit.  You will see kids playing in front of their homes, tons of dogs enjoying their walks, and lots of friendly people who will always say hello.  Just a few blocks away you will find the major commercial Clement & Geary corridor, packed with restaurants, shops, cafes, pharmacies, boutiques, gift shops, service/repair shops, dry cleaners, grocery stores ... and more.  We have a great Farmers Market on Sunday mornings with live music and lots of produce, meats, baked goods, flowers and yummy things to eat while you shop. host_about: I've lived in San Francisco since 1997 and enjoy all the city has to offer: great restaurants, live music and theater, the parks, the best shopping in the world, temperate weather, wine country just 45 minutes away, the ocean and the bay, the Giants, the Warriors and the 49ers. I would love to share info on all my favorite places in the city and give you suggestions based on your interests.

host_about:
My husband and I have recently retired and are loving life!   In the city, we love walks in Golden Gate Park, hopping the Muni to the AT&T Ballpark for the Giants Games, listening to music, reading, and spending time with family in San Francisco.  
We travel and spend time  in our vineyard in the foothills of the Sierra mountains where we enjoy our children, our wines, and our relaxed life after many years in the health care profession.  We have two lovely grandchildren whom we adore and enjoy so much! 
Our favorite restaurants in the area are Ragazza for Italian food, Nopalito for a Tapas style Mexican food, and the Pork Store on Haight Street for the best breakfast Quesadilla in the universe!
We have owned the Victorian Home and have updated it over 40 years; we did a earthquake retrofit on our home and created an amazing space on the lower level complete with 9 foot ceilings, and a wall of glass looking out over our secluded Zen Deck, which is mostly protected from the wind and fog and noise of the city.  We are happy to share our lovely ZEN apartment with you during the times we are out of the city.

We have registered with the city of San Francisco, and our Short Term Rental registration number is STR (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) 
Rosellen and Elliot Krames

In the exterior of the home, I combined California's rich, native foliage to create a garden that is both relaxing and rejuvenating. The house is three-stories: - The ground level has a foyer, dining room, reception area, kitchen, living room, and bathroom. - The second floor is where I have my study that doubles as a room (pull-out sofa), a bathroom adjacent to the office, and the master bedroom (queen bed) and bath.  - There is also a deck with sitting and views of the Golden Gate Bridge and Bay. - Below the ground level is media room with sofa (pull-out queen size sofa-bed), terrace/garden room (with a pull-out queen size sofa-bed) leading to the outside deck, and the garage. The outside deck has two-levels. One is a fire-heated l
neighborhood_overview: Pacific Heights is a historic neighborhood in San Francisco. Home to many of San Francisco's Victorian and Edwardians, you'll get stunning views of Alcatraz, Golden Gate Bridge, and the San Francisco Bay as you travel up and down the hills that make my neighborhood famous.  Centrally located, Union Street is a block away and Chestnut St is five-blocks away. Both are filled with countless restaurants, cafes, bars, and boutiques, all within a short walk of the house.  Downtown SF is a 15-minute drive, Fisherman's Wharf is 10-minutes away, and the Bay is mere minutes away.

neighborhood_overview: While you can visit all of SF and the Peninsula conveniently from our home, we love our neighborhood. We live in Ingleside, an urban and residential neighborhood where you are likely to see commuters walking towards BART in the morning and kids riding their bike in the street in the afternoon. Ocean Ave is just about a mile away where you can access Whole Foods, City Target, some bars and some casual, and delicious, food establishments. From our home, it is very easy to hop on the freeway or BART and head south towards the Peninsula, Silicon Valley and San Jose - you can just as easily head north. We are two BART stops away from the Mission neighborhood and four BART stops from downtown SF (about 10-15 minutes on BART to downtown SF). access: Check-In is via accessing a key in a lockbox: we will send instructions once you book with us. Your room is located in the ground level of our home: your semi-private entrance is through a side gate and side doorway with just a few steps through a garage/basement to your private room and bath. You have a door that locks and you will receive a set of keys to use throughout your stay.  Because your room is at ground level and built into a hill, the plumbing in your bathroom is connected to a sani-flo system. This means that you will hear a pump during and shortly after showering, flushing the toilet and using the sink. Please keep this in mind if you are traveling with a companion who is a light sleeper. Ability to walk up and down stairs is necessary - please ask us if you have mobility concerns, we are happy to answer your questions and make sure that you will feel safe and comfortable in our home.
interaction: We are generally around weeknights and weekends to chat with you in person about any needs or questions you have. If you contact us after 8pm at night, we will not get back to you until the morning hours (around 6am).

neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood is full of things to do, eat and drink.  You have immediate access to many attractions and you are a short walk from Alcatraz Landing where you would catch the ferry to Alcatraz.  We don't sell Alcatraz tickets and they sell out in advance so (Hidden by Airbnb) them if you care to go. notes: Remember you are surrounded by water and you are exposed to one if not many of mother nature's elements at any given time. Please read our reviews and we hope that you will find the feedback you need to understand what to expect.

Parking - use (Hidden by Airbnb) maps on your mobile device - when you search for "parking near pier 39 san francisco ca"  you will get multiple options with distance and price.   7. Multiple car rental agencies within walking distance 8. CA Welcome Center - Upstairs on Pier 39 is an excellent resource for activities, transportation, and they also have a bag check for those who get in early or depart late and need a place to leave bags.
access: You will have access to the whole boat.  Please note that fires of any kind are not allowed on the boat per our insurance. Please respect other boat owners and guests space and privacy.  If there is a sea lion on the finger don't walk down between two boats to look at the sea lion  The space between the two boats is referred to as a finger and the finger is just like someones front yard.

host_about:
I'm an Registered Nurse in the magical city of San Francisco, working in women's health. I'm also a former pastry chef and amateur jeweler and interior designer. My husband Juan Luis is a general contractor, carpenter, and wicked good pool player and is originally from Costa Rica, which is another magical place. We love to cook and eat (vegetarian for me, meat for him), go on long road trips, hunt through antique stores, flea markets, and yard sales, and only rarely go to movies because Juan Luis always falls asleep. We met salsa dancing in 2006 and have been ferociously in love ever since. 

We're crazy about SF's Victorians and feel incredibly lucky to own one. JL has restored and cared for ours painstakingly, and has also painted and restored several of our neighbors' Victorians as well.

Our hosting style is relaxed and we try to give you all the privacy we can while still being available to answer questions, solve any unexpected problems, or make recommendations. We both work a lot, so can't hang out and socialize as much as we might otherwise like, and we hope our guests will be out enjoying the city and Bay Area as well as relaxing in our gorgeous and comfy home.

We wish we had more time for traveling, so we love to live vicariously through our guests and hope you love Hayes Valley and San Francisco as much as we do!

neighborhood_overview: The Mission District is an amazingly vibrant, exciting, and culturally rich neighborhood—it's also SF's largest. Our location (at the intersection of 24th and Potrero) is right on the historic 24th Street Corridor—el Corazón de la Misión—a part of the Mission that retains the unpretentious, creative, culturally rich vibe that first made the neighborhood cool. A 12-minute walk west takes you past bakeries, taquerias, cafés, restaurants, bars, music venues, murals, art galleries, and unique shops to Valencia St, the heart of Mission hipness), and ten solid blocks of the neighborhood's hottest spots—new and old. Along the way, you pass the 24th St BART Station, which offers quick transit to downtown and to surrounding neighborhoods. A 15-minute walk south, on the other hand, takes you up Bernal Hill—worth the climb for one of SF's most epic 360* views—and over to the super chill Bernal Heights neighborhood, home to some of our favorite restaurants and bars. notes: * Parking: there is 1-hour parking available on the street right outside the house or there is a parking garage/lot (SF General Hospital Medical Center Garage), located at 24th and Utah Street (3 blocks from the house) that costs ~$12/day and has hourly rates as well for shorter time periods. * We have a cat—Squirrelly Joe. We call him a "dog-cat" because of his incredibly personable demeanor. If you leave either of your suite doors cracked open, he will almost certainly wander in to say "hello" or sleep on your bed while you're away. If you'd rather he not, a closed door will do the trick. He has free roam of the kitchen, deck, and garden, where you'll often find him sunning himself. As noted above, please be mindful of the front door. He's not a bolter, but if it's left open he might wander out, and it's very important that he stay safely indoors or in the back garden.
transit: The 24th Street BART (underground train) station is a 10–12-minute walk away and there are buses and taxis available just outside the front door. The San Francisco convention center is easily accessible by BART (3 stops) or taxi.   Lyft and Uber are also exceeding affordable from our neighborhood to most parts of the city ($10 or less). You can also rent bikes (the best in the city!) just around the corner from our friends at Dandyhorse, which really frees you to explore all of SF (and they offer our guests a nice discount). (:
access: The split bathroom, accessed in the hallway just outside the master bedroom, is shared with the Airbnb guests in the second bedroom. We provide a selection of toiletry essentials (shampoo, conditioner, body soap) for guest use. The kitchen, deck, and garden are communal spaces (shared also with our very popular cat, Squirrelly Joe). You can choose to hang out in the communal space or have a more private stay—it's entirely up to you. We do not allow guests to cook in the kitchen and we do not provide food beyond breakfast and coffee/tea, but you're more than welcome to keep perishables in the refrigerator or use the microwave to heat up leftovers or other fare. We will also occasionally have friends or family here, who you may run into in communal areas.
interaction: Depending on timing and how on-the-go you are, we may only see each other at check-in or in passing. Occasionally, we're out of town and have a close friend and neighbor who plays host in our absence. Typically, since we both work just out the back door and down the stairs, we are almost always available (and always very happy) to answer questions or share tips on our favorite parts of San Francisco and the Mission District. Squirrelly Joe is always available for conversation and affection, but please be mindful of the front door. He's not a bolter, but if it's left open he might wander out, and it's very important that he stay safely indoors or in the back garden.

Hope to meet you soon,

Laurence

neighborhood_overview: People often ask me if the neighborhood is safe. My answer is yes, except that I wouldn't recommend walking around there late at night. If you need to go to the house after midnight, I recommend taking an Uber rather than the public transportation.   3rd street is the main street with all the businesses in the neighborhood, and it is only a couple of blocks from the house. You will find restaurants, grocery, and drug stores along 3rd street.  The businesses and population are not as dense as downtown San Francisco is, but that also has its benefits (like in finding a parking spot!). Bayview definitely has its own unique character and flavor and charming quirkiness. Take for instance the tiny little "grocery" shop run out of the bottom of a nice lady's house on one of the corners of Lane Street and Newcomb....I admit to having bought a Spiderman popsicle there once or twice...
transit: The house is just two blocks from Third Street, where you can catch the Muni T-line train which runs straight downtown to the Financial District of San Francisco in about 30 minutes. Or, download Uber or Lyft on your phone and order a car to come pick you up and take you wherever you want! Uber Pool and Lyft Line are the shared-ride options offered by Uber and Lyft, which are cheaper but will pick up and drop off other passengers along the way, so it takes longer.
access: There is no private parking at the house, however parking on the street in the neighborhood is free and does not require a permit (rare in San Francisco!). You will have access to the entire house, except other guests' private rooms.
house_rules: 1. Please clean up after yourself when you use the bathroom or kitchen (wash dishes and pans,  wipe hair out of shower/sink, etc.). This way the next person to use them can have a pleasant experience.  2. Please keep things quiet after 10pm and before 8am to respect other housemates who might need to sleep.  3. Please wash your make-up off before you go to bed.  Make-up stains and ruins the sheets/bedding! If the bedding is found stained with make-up after your use, a $50 cleaning/replacement fee will be applied to your reservation.  4. No smoking, candles,  incense, or drugs are permitted in your room (or the house).  A $300 cleaning fee will be charged if you smoke indoors, and your reservation may be canceled.   Also please no parties or heavy drinking.  Thank you so much! Jackie

neighborhood_overview: Our neighborhood is relaxed and safe, located between the Central Richmond and Seacliff districts. Life carries on at a much slower pace than in areas closer to downtown. Out here in the avenues, you'll trade a Starbucks on every corner for mom-and-pop shops, beautiful green spaces, and your pick of neighborhood playgrounds. Stops for major bus lines are less than five minutes away.  Downtown is 20 minutes by car or 35-45 minutes by bus.
notes: The forced air furnace system is shared with our flat above, which is where the thermostat is. The furnace will automatically turn on when the temperature upstairs dips below 68 degrees. For your convenience, there is an oil-filled radiator in the in-law apartment for your use. To those with severe cat allergies, it’s important for you to know that two indoor cats live in the flat above the apartment. They never leave the flat, but since the heating system is shared, it is possible that some allergens may be circulated through your space.  Parking There is no guest parking in the garage or driveway at any time. Street parking can usually be found on our block during the day, except during the school year at drop off time (8:45-9:05 am) and pick up time (3:05-3:25) for the middle school up the street. Please be mindful of street cleaning, which happens every other week. Be sure to carefully read posted signs that detail street cleaning dates and times. Parking permits are not required a
transit: Taking the bus from the neighborhood toward downtown is a great way to tour the northern half of San Francisco.  Muni lines 1 and 38 are your best public transit options for heading east. Trip planners and route maps are available online. A typical ride on the bus to and from downtown varies from 30 minutes to 45 minutes depending on the day of the week and time of day.  You’ll typically wait no longer than five minutes for an Uber to pick you up from our building. An Uber ride to downtown is about 20 minutes without traffic.  The nearest Zipcars are only two blocks away. Typical car rental agencies (Hertz and Enterprise Rent-a-Car) are a short bus ride or 30 minute walk away.
access: Guests have full access to the ground level in-law apartment and to the backyard. Access to the apartment is through the garage, but guests are not allowed to park in the garage or in the driveway.
interaction: The building is home to our family of four and my parents. We live in the flat directly above the ground level in-law apartment and my parents live in the flat above ours. You will no doubt hear my young children (ages 3 and 6) at some point during your stay. It’s possible that you will see children playing in the backyard or someone tending to the plants in the garden. We will not be offended if you close the shades for privacy while we are out there. Likewise, feel free to reach out and chat with us!  If you don't like kids and the noises they make or are looking for absolute quiet during the day, you might be more comfortable staying elsewhere.  FYI: There is a security camera located in the front of the building and another located in the garage. There are no cameras inside the apartment or the backyard.  You are always welcome to text, email, or call with questions or concerns during your stay.
house_rules: Parking As much as I wish we could provide parking to out guests, every parking space at the building is occupied by members of my family that live here full-time. Aside from quick loading and unloading of people and luggage, parking is not allowed in the garage or the driveway. Like most big city dwellers, San Franciscans are protective of their driveways. Many won't hesitate to have your vehicle ticketed or towed if it is blocking just a small portion of their driveway. Please be considerate in how and where you park! Number of Guests The apartment is approximately 500 square feet. The maximum number of guests is four and is best suited to couples, families with young children or a group of close adult friends.  A group of four adults that don't know each other well or families with grown children might find the space a bit tight if they are not accustomed to sharing a bathroom or being in close proximity to each other. Please adjust your expectations accordingly.  Check-in/Check-out

neighborhood_overview: Mission Terrace is a residential neighborhood south of downtown SF. We are one of the few non-hilly neighborhoods in the area which makes walking to our local coffee shops, bars, restaurants and grocery stores a breeze. We're also very close to other neighborhoods like Glen Park, Bernal Heights, Excelsior and Noe Valley.  It is a safe, friendly, and sunny neighborhood. BART rides can get you downtown in 15 minutes.  Urban Wilderness hiking is available 15 minutes away at Glen Canyon Park. City College and SF State are near by as well.
notes: We live upstairs and are typically home during your stay. We do our best to keep noise to a minimum, though there is slight noise heard as we walk down the hallway on our 90 year old wood floors. We keep noise from TV, music and conversation to a minimum between between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. and kindly ask our guests to do the same. We also have two cats who live upstairs with us and you may occasionally hear them greet us when we arrive home. The cats never have access to the unit at any time.

On UberX Express, you can get into Soma for just $1!
access: Guests have access to the property via the garage with a code that we will send you before your arrival. The same code will also open the door to your unit inside the garage. host_about:
I'm a California girl originally from LA. I've lived in Spain, New York and now I've found my way back to my home state and am living in San Francisco. I find it difficult to settle down in places, some might even say I'm a bit of a nomad.  The one constant is that I love to explore and travel to new places. My three favorite companions are my husband Trent and our two cats CC & Gato.  

I've spent a fair amount of time traveling abroad so my eye is currently on planning trips road trips across the continental US in a WV Westfalia Bus. I also would love to go on a culinary tour of Japan and take an extended trip back to Paris. 

When I travel I like to be centrally located, but off the main drag. I don't like going to the must-see places, I want to see where the local people hang. I like to be comfortable, but I prefer to stay in AirBNBs over hotels.  

As a host, I want my guests to feel the same comfort they would feel at home. I typically try to provide some sort of welcome items to help guests feel at ease.

I don't have a life motto, but I believe in gratitude, humility and kindness. I look forward to meeting you, whether as a guest or host.

neighborhood_overview: The spectacular location of this property means you are steps from the action of the Castro, but on a relatively quiet residential block. Dolores park - easily some of the best people-watching in the city - is a short walk, as are a host of restaurants, cafes, bars, and trendy stores of the Mission and Noe. And of course there's BiRite ice cream a few blocks away. The MUNI is around the corner, so head to the newly opened SFMOMA, explore the farmer's market in the ferry building, or shop till you drop at Union Square. But be sure to take a break from sightseeing and chat with the wonderful locals you'll meet along the way. Because San Francisco, perhaps more than any city in the world, is a state of mind.
notes: I'm assuming most guests who are visiting this wonderful city won't notice that this home does not currently have a television. I own an awesome 50" TV that I haven't turned on in years, so it's sitting in the study waiting to be auctioned off! There is a flight of stairs up to the home, so unfortunately this may not be suitable for some guests. Oh and this home is not (yet) child-safe.
transit: Several MUNI and bus lines are a (very) short walking distance from the home.
access: Guests who book this listing will have access to the entire home. The master bedroom has a lot of period architectural features, a queen size bed, and an entire closet for your use. The second bedroom (this is where I would sleep if I were in town) has a king bed and possibly the world’s most comfortable bedding (I take sleep seriously). The bathroom is split – with the shower and tub separate from the toilet, which allows both to be used simultaneously (the Edwardians were onto something). The updated kitchen has modern appliances and pretty much everything you’d need to cook up a fancy meal. The living room is generously sized with plenty of space to kick back and relax over a board game or a glass of wine. There is a patio and a small, shared backyard. I've recently moved into this home, so any feedback on improving the experience for future guests is welcome.
interaction: I am passionate about San Francisco and am happy to share tips about hidden gems and local secrets. I'm happy to grab a drink together and am readily reachable by text or phone. That said, I am a physician and researcher and work long hours, so I am not always around.
house_rules: - I welcome you to my home, and hope you will treat it as respectfully as you would your own. No parties, smoking, drugs, or guns. Although steps away from the historic Castro district, this is a residential block, and midnight to 7am is (relatively) quiet time. No day time or night time hosting - registered guests only please. Thank you!

If you're looking to be surrounded by endless restaurant/coffee/etc options outside your door, our place might not be for you.  We love this neighborhood because it's quiet, flat (so rare in SF!), and central.  SOMA is the startup district. We’re less than two blocks away from Airbnb, Adobe, Pinterest, Zynga, and many other smaller startups and tech conferences. Walking to the Mission, Potrero Hill, the Haight, the Castro or the Downtown Financial District is relatively quick and flat.  Public transit is okay but not great in SOMA. You’ll spend less than $10-15 to get anywhere in San Francisco, usually closer to $5-6. Quiet, peaceful, friendly, sunny, and also boasting some of the best views of San Francisco.  Peralta Park is steps away from the casita, and it offers you a chance to take a break, sit in cement blocks, and marvel at the expansive San Francisco skyline. Its 10-15 min drive to downtown or 12 min walk to the closest BART underground at 24th & Mission, which is 2-3 stops to downtown. neighborhood_overview: Crocker-Amazon is a beautiful neighborhood in San Francisco that borders the Excelsior District and is south of the Mission District. The neighborhood is adjacent to the sprawling Crocker-Amazon Park, named after the Charles Crocker land holdings that once made up the area, and Amazon Street in the Excelsior.  The neighborhood benefits from some of the most varied weather in the city, with a balance of sun and fog. The top of the neighborhood boasts outstanding views of downtown San Francisco in the gap between McLaren Park and Twin Peaks. The diverse architecture of the homes throughout the neighborhood include Marina, Arts & Crafts, Victorian, Edwardian, and Mid-Century Modern styles. Geneva Avenue and Mission Street, which bound the neighborhood, feature a number of great places to eat including Food Network featured burgers at Broken Record or amazing burritos at El Farilito.
transit: The area is well-served by public transportation. MUNI Routes 8X, 8BX, and 54 serve the Geneva Avenue corridor and the 43 bus also serves Geneva Avenue, as well as Naples, Cordova, and Munich Streets. During rush hour, the Balboa Park Bart Station is only about a five-minute drive, an eight-minute bus ride, or a 15-minute walk. The neighborhood is convenient to nearby Interstate 280, and to the Alemany Boulevard thoroughfare.
interaction: We love the city and are happy to answer questions and offer suggestions on things to see and do in this fun city.

In my travels, I have stayed at some amazing places and know what a difference great hospitality can make to a trip. I therefore strive to create an experience at Standout Stays that will be memorable and unique. My aim is that you will come back each time you return to San Francisco to stay here again.

If you are considering booking one of my listings, I know you will love your stay here!

If I have made a reservation request with you, I can promise that you will be delighted to have me as a guest.

Hope to meet you soon,

Laurence

Greetings!

My name is Warren C. Lathe III, I go by Trey (a nickname, means "3" :). I am a career biologist (molecular genetics) though currently, I'm writing, teaching and other things (like Airbnb!). 

My partner in crime since 1996, and legal husband since 2008, is Guy and we have two school-age (middle and high schools) children (the picture here was 8 years ago :D). Guy is an English as a Second Language teacher by training and career, but now manages properties.

His GGrandfather was Jose de los Santos Berryessa.  Guy's parents were married and lived in this city during the '40s (while his father fought in the Pacific theater). My own parents moved to the Bay Area in the 80's. Guy and I both moved into this home in 1997. San Francisco had been our dream city for its acceptance, tolerance, family heritage and its beauty. It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

A fifteen minute walk will take you to Cortland Avenue, a lovely shopping street complete with healthy grocery market, unique gift store, yoga, massage, library, bank and art galleries. We provide our guests with privacy while also offering travel and local recommendations based upon our 36 years as San Franciscans.  We love meeting new people and making new friends.

Skate and I have travelled extensively throughout Europe, Asia, Middle East, Africa and North, Central and South America. We love to explore back roads, back alleys and back woods. We can be exhausting to travel with! 

One of our favorite things to do is to travel simply and affordably by either camping or staying in homes so that we get to really experience the culture and people of the region we are visiting.
 
We enjoy spending time in our garden and with our family, we also enjoy eating good food, traveling to new and exciting destinations, camping, sunshine and live music which you may hear Skate playing!
 
For us Airbnb is a wonderful way to travel but also through hosting a way to meet new people from all over the world while staying at home!

Skate and I look forward to meeting you!

space: Built in 1900, this property is a true part of San Francisco history. Throughout the years, the house has served several purposes: recording studio where songs for artists such as Elton John, En Vogue, and the Whispers were recorded; karate dojo where, among others, the legendary Black Panthers trained; and home to one of the first internet radio stations in the country. This house has brought much joy to those of us who have been lucky enough to live and work here, and I hope it can bring you the same.

Pacific Heights is a quiet, up-scale residential area rising up from San Francisco Bay, minutes from the Golden Gate Bridge and central to all major city sites.  The bustling neighborhood street of Fillmore (four blocks away) has top-rated restaurants to fit any budget, cafes, coffee shops, bars, boutiques. notes: This is a great neighborhood and I love it and my neighbors! The BART (our subway) is a 15-20 minute walk and buses are as close as a block away. Uber (and Lyft!) are good options as well. Because the area is relatively flat (especially for San Francisco) biking is a good option. It is flat from the apartment, all throughout the Mission, to downtown, even Fisherman's Wharf if you take the proper route. Bike lanes run throughout the city. There is ample storage for bicycles in the hallway that leads to the room.

The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. 'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

The Richmond is home to a vast affluent Chinese population and its commercial strips on Geary Blvd. and Clement Street are commonly referred to as the second Chinatown and boasts more highly rated Chinese restaurants than Chinatown itself.  The Richmond also has deep Irish and Russian roots and has many Catholic and Orthodox churches.

Grab sundries at Apple, Walgreens or Safeway.  Stroll to the Golden Gate Bridge, Palace of Fine Arts, Chrissy Field, or Fisherman's Wharf.  SHOPPING!!! Cow Hollow. Drinks at Tipsy Pig. TV with local channels only (no cable) forces you to get out and enjoy SF, and not be a couch potato. Blazing fast 100MB/sec Comcast Internet accessible via WiFi! Laser printer (b&w Samsung ML-2510) and color scanner (Epson Perfection 2580) on a cart roll out of the closet if you need to be productive. Home office includes chair, desk and 24" monitor w/Thunderbolt connections for your Mac. Tons of power outlets on both sides of entertainment cart. Use of Apple charging cable on nightstand. Amazon Echo answers your questions ("Alexa, what's the weather today?") Full kitchen if you desire (but get out and eat, there are so many great restaurants within a 2 minute walk and it IS San Francisco). Fridge to keep your snacks cold, help yourself to anything in there.

neighborhood_overview: You can't go wrong with most of the neighborhoods in San Francisco, however, the Marina has a charm all of its own.  Chestnut street is always full of wandering locals enjoying many of the restaurants that the neighborhood has to offer.  Two movie theaters and walking access to the water, GG Bridge and Fishermans's Wharf make this the most charming neighborhood, in my opinion.  Rent bicycles from 1 block away and bike across the Golden Gate Bridge then take the ferry back.
notes: Like most buildings in San Francisco, the electrical has not been fully updated.  While I don't expect there to ever be an issue, if by some chance you overload the electrical, you may need to replace fuses, which I provide. It's not something to worry about, but I would advise you to be mindful of using more than ONE electricity draining appliances at the same time (microwave, hairdryer, etc.). Normal devices (TV, lights, laptop, phone chargers, etc.) are not an issue. Guitar and bicycle shown in photos no longer available in the unit.
transit: Bus routes on Chestnut (30 North Beach to the ballpark), Fillmore (22 to the Mission) and Union Street (41 & 45 to North Beach & Financial District & BART) make getting anywhere a breeze.  I highly suggest you download and install a ridesharing app like Lyft (URL HIDDEN) or Uber (URL HIDDEN) and add your credit card ("shared" carpooling rides get you anywhere in the city for ~$6 for two people).  These apps make getting around SF soooo much better and avoid the headaches of hailing cabs, which are non-existent in SF.  Also, if you are able bodied there are rideshare mopeds (Scoot), scooters (Lime, Bird) and bikes abundantly in the neighborhood, so install the apps in advance (you can injure yourself so please be careful and I do not advocate using these modes of transportation).
access: You will have full access to the entire studio. Quarter operated $2 each: washer & dryer are downstairs near the recycling and trash bins.
interaction: While I'll be away traveling, I'm always available via text to provide recommendations or to answer any questions about the space.  I want your stay to be great!
house_rules: - No pets (prefer no pet owners as I have strong allergies to latent pet hair) - Prefer you remove shoes once you enter the unit.  - Quiet hours after 10 pm. - No parties or events allowed as this is a quiet building. - Storing bags/luggage before/after check-in is not guaranteed; plan on storing bags at "California Welcome Center - PIER 39"   (URL HIDDEN)
host_about: Native Coloradoan living in SF. I love where I live in the Marina, and so will you. Marketer by trade, Mechanical Engineer by training I love to build and you'll see accents of this throughout my space, from the custom wood entertainment center that cozies up perfectly against the bay window to the LED lighted floor length closet mirror that lights up when you step in front of it.  My space is a reflection of who I am -  Maker. Neat. Contemporary. Looking forward to hosting your SF adventure.

neighborhood_overview: Bayview, San Francisco is a neighborhood that represents decades of African-American culture. It features a lot of solid community culture; great people, great music, great community feeling, and obviously great soul/Southern food. Today, it is one of SF’s most diverse districts, with lots of families and professionals from multi-ethnic backgrounds. It’s one of the city’s hidden gems, and I’m happy it’s that way right now, but also looking forward to the future where it evolves.
transit: We're conveniently located 15 min from SFO, and a 20 min Uber ride to downtown SF.  Uber Pool is the cheapest and fastest way to get around the city. You can also walk 1.5 blocks down our hill to 3rd/La Salle to take the T-train downtown to SOMA and Financial District. If you rent a car, there's plenty of free parking half a block away. Just watch out for street sweeping and don’t block any driveways.

neighborhood_overview: Bernal Heights is an urban village built onto a hill.  As a result, it is one of the more magical neighborhoods of San Francisco.  Walks in Bernal Heights include numerous stairway streets, hidden mini-parks and gardens, panoramic views of the city and the bay, and frequent opportunities for refreshment breaks at corner stores, cafes, restaurants and bars. This is an urban hiker’s paradise! To really get the full neighborhood experience you’ll have to take it off-roading since some areas are only accessible by foot, but even if you stick to streets you’ll still fall in love with the whimsical charm around every corner.  There are numerous coffee shops in the immediate vicinity, and the famous Mitchell's ice cream is just two blocks away. If you are craving a San Francisco burrito, Taqueria Can-Cun is just around the corner.  Some other noteworthy restaurants just a stone's throw away are Baby Blues BBQ, The Front Porch (soul food), Blue Plate (new-style American), ICHI+NI (sushi bar),

We are always respectful and aware that we are sharing our space with guests, and we act accordingly. If you plan to drive or rent a car while staying with us, and you do not expect to use it during the weekdays, you should be prepared to park two or three blocks away from the house, at a minimum. transit: We are conveniently located on the northwest corner of Bernal Heights, just a block away from vibrant Mission St.  We are close enough to be able to walk to a large variety of restaurants, bars and performance venues, but far enough to not have to deal with too much noise.  The public transportation is easy and quick: We are a block away from the 14/49 bus stop, a 10 minute walk from the 24th and Mission BART station, and 15 minutes from the J-Church street car.  There are also numerous parks – large and small – amazing walks, incredible views and many other lively commercial strips to take in without ever having to drive. This is the perfect spot for travelers who want to simply come home to a comfortable nest, as well as those who wish to spend time exploring locally in one of San Francisco’s favorite neighborhoods.

neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Marie is a longtime resident of San Francisco (55 years). She was born in Hong Kong and raised in São Paulo, Brazil until she moved to The City at the age of 16. She and her late husband were married for 28 years before he passed away in 1995. Marie has raised both her daughters in this listed Diamond Heights home, now 35 & 45 years old. We live here part time so one closet has our belongings but other spaces are entirely at your disposal. That also means that we maintain it scrupulously and attend to problems promptly. The wifi has a new router and the TV plays cable, DVDs, and Amazon, Netflix, Hulu, etc. All the makings for coffee are here and the kitchen is fully equipped.

neighborhood_overview: The old Dolores Mission church is nearby and the Castro district's just a 15-minute walk away. Dolores Park, with great views of downtown, lots of grass for relaxing, and tennis courts for playing, is three blocks and Valencia Street is foodie heaven. Whole Foods and Safeway are a quick walk; restaurants, bars and shops abound, and public transit stations are only a short walk away. Ramona is a quite, tree-lined, one-way steet close to everything but quiet and safe.
notes: The building, and this quiet little street, date to 1912. Before that it was pasture for Mission Dolores, one of the original Spanish missions. The apartment has been beautifully renovated and has all modern conveniences. It also has the original wood flooring and wavy, hand fashioned glass in dining room cabinets and the front windows. The fireplace is not functional and can't be used but it adds to the charm of the dining room.
transit: MUNI and the bus or subway lines, or BART are in easy reach.  Walking will take you almost anywhere. The "F" MUNI trolley stops nearby and will take you, above ground, to the waterfront and all the attractions there from the Ferry Building to Fisherman's Wharf. Even downtown is just a 40 minute stroll down Market Street or a 10-15 minute MUNI ride. Five different lines stop just a couple of blocks away so there is seldom more than a few minute wait for a train. Downtown, Union Square, the Embarcadero, Civic Center and the symphony, ballet and opera are two subways stops away. Bikes or cars can be rented nearby.
access: Breakfast isn't provided but everything you need to prepare meals is here from coffee to condiments and cook books. Meals can be made at home as much as you wish. Some food supplies and a full range of cooking implements are available. But the number of nearby restaurants may make you think twice about cooking at home!

neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Historically known for its large African-American population, people from all walks of life live in the Bayview -- from doctors, lawyers, and teachers to construction workers, custodians, and artists. Unlike other neighborhoods, you'll see all ethnicities represented in the Bayview. We have had guests dock us on stars for location citing the "rough neighborhood," which we feel is unfair. If you are uncomfortable in a historically African-American neighborhood with people from many different socio-economic and ethnic backgrounds, this is really not the place for you.  That said, the sun is particularly strong here. It pushes the infamous fog to the other parts of the city! We are a family of four doing the best we can to stay in this breathtaking, but increasingly expensive city. Ken has lived here almost all his life. Chloe has lived here half of her life. Gemma and Freya, the most charming girls ever, were both born here and will hopefully make San Francisco their home when they grow up.

Ken is a government employee, and Chloe works for a labor organization. Gemma is a four year old who is currently attending preschool. Freya is a two year old who grandma takes care of during the day.

We began using Airbnb back in 2013. We can't stop saying good things about the platform, which enabled us to travel to far away locales for reasonable prices and explore as the locals would.

We know the City probably as well as (and likely better than) any native. We enjoy cooking and exploring new restaurants and parks. 

In opening our home to the world, we are obviously looking to earn some extra money to enable us to stay in San Francisco. But that's not our only motivation, as there are many other ways to make money. Part of our reason is to enable Gemma and Freya to potentially be exposed to people from different parts of the world and to teach them the value of experiencing the world through travel when they grow up. neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. neighborhood_overview: Mission Gulch offers the best of San Francisco - a great mx of old-timers and up-and-comers.  There are a lot of great places within 5 minutes walk:  Sightglass for great coffee, Tartine Manufactory for incredible bread, Heath Ceramics for beautiful, locally crafted artisanal home goods, Trick Dog for signature cocktails.   Ten minutes walk gets you to everything else that the Mission has to offer:  movies at the Alamo Theater, dinners at Foreign Cinema, freshly made tortillas from Ka Palma Mexicatessan, lazy weekend days at Dolores Park, extraordinary yumminess at Mission Cheese, insane chocolate and Dandelion, and ice cream at Bi Rite.
transit: If you have a car - we are a quick 15-minute trip from the Airport - just off the 280 and 101.  So everything beyond San Francisco is easily accessible.  Parking anywhere in San Francisco can be tricky business - so if you plan to rent a car, it's best to rent something as small as possible. Lyft - our trusty car-sharing app - is usually at our door within 1 to 3 minutes. Muni - San Francisco's bus system - has stops on either side, just 2 to 3 blocks away. interaction: Chances are, if you're staying in our house, we're off to some other location.  That said, we have friends nearby, and try to make ourselves as reachable as possible so we can ensure a quality stay.
house_rules: - This is city living, so we are a no-shoes house.  Also - please no parties - we have neighbors on all sides whom we want to continue to call friends!
