host_about:
Sharing spaces that I have designed is both a business and a passion with this year marking my 20th season in Lake Tahoe.  Over the years many rental clients have become good friends and return each year to the same property.  Being the host to these return guests is the most rewarding part of my vacation and short term rental work. .

After spending my adult years raising my family on a sheep farmlett in Sebastopol California  with summer and weekend visits to  Lake Tahoe, got the travel bug and found an opportunity for change so change happened.

Buenos Aires is where I now spend about half of my time, por razon de tango (because of tango) but also because it is a fun and with the internet my work can happen wherever I am in the world.  Argentina is a  random place where strange things always happen.  I have met wonderful, interesting international people who come annually to Argentina to immerse themselves in the tango culture.  My life here is a combination of a Danielle Steele romance novel and a Woody Allen Movie. Taking notes, there is a book in here somewhere.

I have always loved dancing and for the last 10 years it has been a huge part of my life. Now that my children are super responsible adults, it has been possible to pursue it on a more intense level.  Ever since I went to college in Spain, living in a Spanish speaking country had always been my desire. I was invited to Buenos Aires in January 2009 to help teach Lindy Hop, specifically Balboa, at an International Lindy Hop Festival. Went tango dancing one night to Club Gricel and got completely hooked during one tanda de Calo, a composer of romantic tangos. A tanda is a group of 3-4 songs with some type of commonality that you dance with one partner. Tango either speaks to you or it does not, hard to explain but what the locals dance is not the show tango that people usually think of, it is a more personal and intimate experience. 

It has been exciting and never boring living a gypsy lifestyle, being able to travel to cities with varied dance communities, always running into friends from my dance world, managing the rentals all day and tango dancing all night, literally.   Sleep sometimes suffers a bit.  My favorite places to visit (and dance) so far have been Istanbul, Cosquin in Argentna for the annual Folklore festival, Rome, and Paris.  Culturally Turkey was the most amazing trip.  My motto has always been "Press On" but at this very moment staying home is sounding like a fun thing! 

Asides from dancing (swing, salsa, tango, folklore, pretty much everything) I also love to cook so every kitchen is fully equipped.  Hiking, skiing, decorating, design work and music are also my passions.  Read a lot more before tango but still find some time to read.  Suggestions are welcome!

Just rented my first property on Air bnb and it was a great experience, cute beach apartment in Venice California.  This inspired me to list on this site.

In order to keep things running smoothly and also to enjoy all that Northern California has to offer I come back several times a year.  When in the California I go through each San Francisco flat and Tahoe house make sure that all is in order and in good repair. To to be able to offer to visitors to Lake Tahoe and San Francisco lovely spaces where they can enjoy their valuable vacation or  time away from home for a project is a pleasure.

house_rules: - - Our house rules are pretty simple: Please be respectful…of the house, the hosts, and your fellow guests. Rule #7: Check out the written caption for the bedroom photo; there have been updates.  Thanks so much for your cooperation! We want each and every one of our guests to have an enjoyable stay with us.
host_about:
Welcome to our home in the vibrant Mission District of San Francisco. We are a professional couple (Angela is a tech/lifestyle public-relations executive; Brian runs a media/entertainment company), with two loving rescue dogs—Bijoux (a Maltipoo) and Jacques (a Westie).

On weekends, you’ll find us exploring San Francisco’s diverse neighborhoods—searching for the best cappuccino, checking out the latest museum and gallery exhibit, and trying out the latest brunch hot spot. In addition, we love traveling, playing tennis, and watching foreign films.

Two of our favorite mottos:
Have courage and be kind.
Eat well and travel often.

We love to meet new, interesting people from all over the world, and we are excited to welcome you to San Francisco and into our home.

Also, the weather and views can't be beat. We are on a quiet street, on the SW side of the hill, closer to the Mission and the hospital. 1/2 mile (easy downhill walk) from the hustle of the Mission District. If you'd prefer to drive, we have ample street parking and one dedicated spot for our guests (**Street cleaning Wednesday at noon is the only time you will need to move the car for approx 2 hours**). And as much as I love climbing the hills (we're like mountain goats here!), you can easily drive and park around Potrero's adorable main street (18th) if you don't feel like hiking. Note: while we are close to the Mission, UCSF Mission Bay, Zuckerberg Hospital (6 min walk), the Dogpatch and SOMA, we are 5 miles (8km) from Fisherman's Wharf/Pier 39 - there is a bus on the corner that will take you there, - slowly - but just know tha
notes: We don't have kids, but we do have an indoor/outdoor cat called Marvin. Though we keep him out of the guest room (even when it's not occupied), if you're allergic, you may want to take this under consideration. Marvin is extremely friendly, and always available for cuddles. We also rarely, but occasionally, dog sit my dad’s chihuahua, and have friends who may visit with dogs. Although we don’t have our own dog, there’s always a chance we may have one visiting. Also, please be sure to familiarize yourself with the lockbox instructions BEFORE arriving. It’s easy, but it’s important! REGISTERED PERMIT FOR SHORT-TERM RENTALS: SAN FRANCISCO STR (Phone number hidden by Airbnb)
transit: Uber/Lyft are usually a 1-2 minute wait. There are several bus stops nearby, but it costs the same and is far faster to use Uber Pool or Lyft Line. Trust us on this one.  The number 19 bus (to "the center" and Market Street and ultimately Fisherman's Wharf), is a block away.  24th Street BART is a mile/20 min walk through the Mission. CalTrain is a little less than a mile, but on the other side of the hill.  UCSF Mission Bay is 1.2 miles away, but the UCSF Shuttle is a ~5 min walk down the hill from our house, just outside SF General.  101 and 280 to Palo Alto/San Jose/points south are easily accessed from the hill.  If you have a car, you can park in our driveway as long as you wish during the week so as to avoid the 1 hour parking restriction (Monday-Friday). The only time there might be an issue are Wednesdays 12-2pm, when cars must be moved to the other side of the street for street cleaning.
access: You're welcome to use all of our communal spaces. There is a kettle, french press, coffee and tea in your room, but you are always welcome to join us downstairs in the dining room. You are also welcome to use our refrigerator (we provide milk, soymilk and cream -help yourself), but we just ask that you don't use the kitchen for cooking.  In addition to the small balcony in your room, there are 2 additional patios and a deck for outside enjoyment. Our back patio has a gas fire pit, where it's easy to kill a few hours in the evening by the fire (please don’t hesitate to ask me to light it for you!) You'll have your own set of keys, so you can come and go as you please. **Parking** is really easy on our street (really!), but restricted to 1 hour from 8am-6pm everywhere EXCEPT our driveway, where you will park. From time to time, because we now have an electric car, we may need to park our car in our own space overnight in order to charge the car.  Honestly, it sounds more complicated than
interaction: I work from home, and you'll usually find me at my desk (the kitchen table) in the morning, available to answer any questions you might have. We're also very social, and often out in the evening, but when we're not, we're happy to have a chat and share a drink with you. Our "quiet" hours are 11pm-7am Monday-Thursday, but please understand that our home is very open and airy, and sound travels. While we are not "party people," and pretty much never throw big parties, we may have friends over for dinner, or we might come home a little late on weekends. However, we do try to keep things generally quiet. :-)
house_rules: - We ask that you take your shoes off inside the house.  - This is a residential building with owners present. We cannot tolerate parties or uninvited guests. Please understand this, or you will be asked to leave.  - Please familiarize yourself with the lockbox check in instructions before arriving (especially if you won’t have access to data here). We are not always home when our guests arrive and hate to leave you standing outside! - Sadly we've had problems with guests overstaying, so we have to state clearly: Overstaying (as defined in Airbnb's Terms of Service) past the check-out time will result in charges at a minimum of $40 per hour of Overstay up to the maximum rate allowed in the Airbnb Terms of Service.    We can often accommodate requests to store luggage for you when needed, feel free to ask in advance!
host_about:
Jennifer Stebner and Daniel Fineman

We're nice folks, easy going, and always leave our Air BnBs as we found them.  We've both in SF 20 years and still love discovering and sharing new corners of our city. Dan is a rock climbing junkie and I love being out on the water. Marvin is everyone's favorite cat! :-)

neighborhood_overview: August and September are wonderful months in the sunny Mission District of San Francisco. Dolores Park, just below our flat, is the scene of outdoor theatre and movies, birthday parties and more, and the best ice cream stands in the city are just off the park. A few blocks away is Valencia Street, where the eating and shopping possibilities can tempt anyone to linger. A free walking tour of the Mission by CityGuides (see their website) every Sunday at 11 am begins at the Golden Fire Hydrant right below our living room window.
transit: While the Muni J streetcar stops just doors away, walking to restaurants, shops and amenities is a pleasant way to move about the City. Twenty minutes on The J will get you downtown to the Embarcadero, but a downhill walk will get you there in an hour or so. A couple of people on our block make this walk to the Financial District every weekday!
access: Our flat is on the third floor—39 steps from the sidewalk. The intercom/buzzer will allow you to open the door to your guests without descending all the way to the landing.  While all three condo units have equal access to the roof deck, we are generally the primary users of the space. The planter boxes on the roof are ours, and are filled with herbs that you are welcome to use if you are cooking—we have rosemary, thyme, mint, sage and oregano. The grill is yours to use. Our visitor parking permit will allow you to park on the street.
interaction: As this is our home, we are only offering it to guests when we are on vacation. Therefore our friend / neighbor / House Manager Laura will be helping you during your stay. Once your booking is confirmed, we will provide her contact information.

host_about:
My wife Barbara and I are both world travelers. We met while in the Peace Corps in Central Africa. We recently retired—Barbara from a career in international development and I from a career in finance and philanthropy. Now we're hoping to travel a bit more consistently and to share our home with you, with the assistance of our wonderful friends in the neighborhood. Among our destinations this summer, both in the Rocky Mountains, are a Peace Corps reunion and a gathering of friends to view the solar eclipse. We've got deep ties to this area, though we are both native Midwesterners (from northern Ohio). It's easy to fall in love with the beauty of this place, when you see the view from our flat. We're both active runners and cyclists, and we volunteer regularly. 

Barbara is a volunteer gardener and garden docent in for the historic Gardens of Alcatraz—check out the gardens themselves or search online for "Alcatraz Gardens"! If you'd like a sit-down activity, Michael is a cruciverbalist (a crossword puzzle constructor) whose work has been published in number of periodicals, including the New York Times. He also does a crossword for the Noe Valley Voice, the free paper in the neighborhood next to us (which you should definitely visit). He also publishes a variety crossword at GardenPartyCrosswords.

neighborhood_overview: Our home straddles two neighborhoods:  The Haight-Ashbury, which is fun, funky, and sometimes smells like a Dead concert, and Ashbury Heights, ruled by stately homes with impeccably manicured frontages and spotless sidewalks.  On Haight street, you will probably be offered drugs and encounter homeless/street people.  While this can be intimidating, these folks are harmless, and the neighborhood is actually quite safe.  In the rest of the neighborhood, expect tree-lined streets, beautiful Victorian homes, and lovely neighbors.  There are two Farmers' Markets in the neighborhood (Wednesdays and Sundays), and every Thursday, Off the Grid (gathering of about a dozen food trucks and live music) meets just 5 blocks away.  Beyond that, it's just a fantastic, vibrant neighborhood that has a little bit of everything.  We like cocktails at Alembic, fancy Mexican at Padrecito, Burgers and beer at Black Sands, and gourmet ice cream at Ice Cream Bar (each just a few blocks from the house).
transit: The city is very accessible via Uber (cars are often 2-3 minutes away) and Muni/Bus; there are bus -stops for 5 routes within one block of the home.  Street parking doesn't require a residential sticker (rare for the city), and is not timed (watch out for weekly street-cleaning signs though).   This part of the city is also relatively flat, and a number of charming street districts (Cole Valley, NOPA, Alamo Square) are walkable.
access: Guests will have access to the whole home, including the TV, Wi-Fi, laundry, and kitchen appliances (including dishwasher).  There's a small "library" of books to read in the Jack-and-Jill powder room.
interaction: We'll be out of the country during your stay, but two on-the-ground folks (my sister-in-law and mother-in-law) will be available to help, should the need arise.  We also love to give detailed recommendations for things to do in the area during your visit; just tell us what you’re interested in and we’ll give you the inside scoop.

neighborhood_overview: Oceanview, also referred to as "Lakeview" by some natives of the community, has a rich history.  Oceanview was originally an Italian-Irish-German neighborhood in the mid- to late nineteenth century; the location acted as a station for train service between San Francisco and San Jose, owned by San Francisco and San Jose Railroad, bought by Southern Pacific in 1868.  Post World War II the Ocean View was one of the few places in San Francisco where African-American families could buy property. During redevelopment in the Western Addition/Fillmore in the 1960s and 70s, more African-American families moved to the neighborhood from the Western Addition and Bayview neighborhoods.  Until the mid-1990s, African Americans accounted for over 50 percent of the neighborhood's residents. In the early 2000s, lower real estate prices relative to the rest of the city brought in a new influx of Asians, Latinos, and Caucasians, making Oceanview one of the most culturally diverse neighborhoods in San Fran

neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis.  Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden. We recommend: - Eating at a one of the delicious restaurants or food trucks, or catch

summary: A sunny and private in-law suite with adjacent deck awaits your arrival in San Francisco's Sunset District. The space in this historic and immaculately decorated Rousseau home includes a foyer; a large room with Queen bed, couch, table/desk and wet bar with mini fridge and coffee/tea fixings; a large bathroom with shower; and a spacious deck beyond which lies the Pacific Ocean. space: This is a great home-base in a charming and quiet local neighborhood from which to explore San Francisco, seek respite from a busy day of meetings or recharge from life with your kids and grandkids. The in-law suite is on the ground floor of my two-story house, and you will have a private entrance off the back of the garage. Here, you will enjoy bright days and cozy nights with plenty of room to stretch out. Just like a hotel room, I provide coffee and tea fixings as well as a tiny fridge but no kitchen or food prep equipment. There is ample delivery service and plenty of options within walking distance, but San Francisco is a food Mecca so I encourage you to really get out and explore! While there is no access to the rest of the house upstairs, you will have everything you need downstairs.

notes: This would be a great spot for a longer stay if you are a business person or a new grandparent, etc. While I don’t normally offer more than a week, message me and I may be able to accommodate multiple weeks/months. transit: With an 83 Walkscore, you are close to the action.  Walk to Harvest Hills Market, Precita Park Cafe, Hillside Supperclub, and two corner markets.  24th Street and all of its amenities start at just three blocks away.   All forms of shared and public transport are also right in the neighborhood.  Rent bikes at Ford GoBike station, electric bikes at Scoot, and cars at Zipcar.   24th Street BART Station is a 20 minute walk away.  One bus ride takes you to Union Square and the Cable Cars. Proximity to the 101 and 280 makes for quick freeway access to and from SFO, Silicon Valley and Wine Country.   It also makes things super easy and quick for Lyft/uber. access: Your area on the first floor is fully stocked for a great stay - even if you don't take advantage of the common area upstairs. I’m available to help you make the most of your stay whether you are a first time visitor or a seasoned business traveler.  If you just need a place to sleep, your space on the first floor is completely private and carefully appointed so you immediately feel at home.  You’ll be able to use all of its amenities without any interaction with me.   If you are more social, I love meeting new people - especially over food and drinks in the evenings.

Street parking is sometimes available, but I recommend the nearby parking garages with overnight and long-term parking options low as $20/night. The bus is highly accessible, as well, though may get crowded often and is not as reliable as BART. host_about:
Mavis and Carole have lived in this gracious and welcoming 2 story Queen Anne home since 1986, and have furnished it to reflect our love of art, books, music and comfort. It is designed for socializing, relaxing and enjoying a view that still makes us pinch ourselves from time to time.
Mavis was raised in Atlanta, Georgia in a family of art and music lovers. After a fulfilling career as a Psychotherapist, she now spends her time traveling, enjoying mostly classical performing arts in San Francisco and in Manhattan, where we have a tiny studio pied-a-terre. Her only regrets about being away from San Francisco are missing our amazing neighbors, and not being able to play her Vintage Mason & Hamlin Baby Grand Piano.
Carole grew up in California and then moved with her family to Memphis, TN. She was able return to Northern California to attend Mills College. Now happily retired from real estate finance, she spends her time cooking, entertaining and planning trips. Like Mavis, she is crazy about New York, and would happily live at Lincoln Center. (Well, Broadway, too.)
Mavis and Carole have swapped houses in Barcelona, Sitges, Berlin, Paris, and Dully, Switzerland (near Lake Geneva.) Our home has gotten wonderful reviews and we have made friends with several of our fellow swappers. 
We love our home, our neighborhood, and our beautiful city by the bay. We look forward to sharing them with our guests.

neighborhood_overview: Walk across the street and up four houses?  You are at Lands End, one of San Francisco’s Hidden Treasure hikes.  Stroll down to our favorite sunset spot.  Or further up and over the hill to Miles Beach.  Or all the way to Sutro Baths, breakfast at Louie’s, or lunch at The Cliff House. In the other direction, stroll down El Camino Del Mar to either China Beach (a five minute walk) or Baker Beach with dramatic views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the Marin Headlands (a fifteen minute stroll). The Palace of Legion of Honor Museum is just up the hill from us, about a two minute drive. You won’t believe you’re still in the city of San Francisco when you stay in Sea Cliff.  We call our beautiful neighborhood “The Amalfi Coast of the West.”
notes: This is a very tactile house.  Remove your shoes upon arrival and step onto the stairs.  Soft leather treads and handrails carry you up to paradise.  Silver jewelry on your way up are part of your artistic experience.   A Tadelakt Moroccan kitchen island serves as our formal reception.  Join other guests in the living room and sit by the fire with a book.  There are five seating areas.  Or open the leather doors behind the Spanish leather bench and you’ll find a television to watch your favorite show.
transit: It used to take taxis 20-30 minutes to get out to our neck of the woods.  Now Uber or Lyft will pick you up in 2-5 minutes! From here to The Ferry Building or downtown San Francisco it will take you twenty minutes by car. There is easy street parking plus a dedicated space in front of Casa al Mare.  We recommend renting a car, so that you can drive over to the Marin Headlands to experience the beautiful view you’ve been looking at.   For the hearty cyclist who is not afraid of hills we will share with you our favorite path to Hawk Hill, Rodeo Beach and/or The Marina, Golden Gate Park, Ocean Beach Sausalito, Mt. Tamalpais, and our favorite Mill Valley / Muir Woods loop. Whether in a car, an Uber or on a bicycle we have lots of fun adventures and favorite picnic spots to share!

neighborhood_overview: The Excelsior is one of the less expensive neighborhoods in San Francisco. There aren’t many hip restaurants or coffee places here, but a lot of good, cheap places to eat and a couple of bars. The neighborhood is very diverse and very safe on this side of McLaren Park, the city‘s 2nd largest parks. A great place to walk or run with great views of the city and the bay, it’s just a few block up the street. We are close to the SFO airport, usually the drive takes about 15min.

access: Kids under the age of 5 are not recommended, as this is not really a kids safe place. You may climb up to the tower and have roof access by my permission only and at your own risk. interaction: We like having guests and will treat you like room mates. But we won't bother you, if you prefer.
house_rules: This is a private home. We live here and share our living space with you. As much as we enjoy having guests and meeting people, we ask you to be respectful to our home and our belongings.  We don‘t recommend stay here with your young kids under the age of 5 years, as this is not really all child prove and you will have to watch your Child at all time very closely. The stair case is very long and high and dangerous and there are artist workshops downstairs with all kinds of things lying around like paint brushes, paint, tools or something alike. Other than that, welcome to our house. Please don‘t hesitate to ask us for anything you need.
host_about: I moved to San Francisco 10years ago from Hamburg, Germany together with Jochen. 2 years ago we fell in love with the old firehouse and now live here together with our 5 year old son and a couple of artists working in their studios downstairs in the former Engine hall. We spend most of our weekends outdoors, kite surfing, hiking, stand up paddle boarding or mountain biking occasionally. Sometimes we decide to improving something in the house (which is a never ending but fun story), or playing some deep house tunes (Jochen), woodworking (me), shooting stop motion movies (Konrad) or playing with Legos. We also sometimes host an event like a movie night, a fundraiser for some important political organization like Southern Poverty law center or shoot a movie to support the Golden Pudel Club in Hamburg.

neighborhood_overview: Our home is in Bernal Heights. We are on the North-West corner, and our home has a view of both Twin Peaks and Downtown. Bernal Heights is hilly, with great views, some steep streets, stairways and tiny parks tucked into side streets. From the park at the top of our hill, there is a 360-degree view of the City, including the bay, the Bay Bridge, the Golden Gate bridge, Twin Peaks, Downtown, Mt Diablo and south to the airport. During baseball season fireworks are often visible from our hill. There is a very sweet commercial street with restaurants, shops and a library. Several parks are nearby for strolling, playing, picnicking and dogs. Our neighborhood is south of the Mission neighborhood, but still within walking distance of the lively nightlife there. It is quieter and cleaner than some of the Mission streets, but not so far from the center that anything is difficult to get to. Bernal Heights was voted America's Hottest Neighborhood in 2014 on the real estate site Redfin
notes: There is an additional guest suite on the ground floor with its own entrance and completely separate.  This may be rented by others, but as of this writing, you could also rent the small studio for another 2-person accommodation!  Perfect for a multi-generational family vacation!

You can also take either a bus or BART train to connect to CalTrain to get down to Silicon Valley, Stanford or San Jose. (I ride my bike to the CalTrain station every day.) You can get to and from the SFO or OAK airport on BART. Mission St and Valencia St in the Mission neighborhood are walking distance. Cortland Avenue, our quaint neighborhood commercial district is a few blocks away as well. Essential services like laundry, groceries, coffee, restaurants, ice cream and several parks are within a couple of blocks. A determined pedestrian could easily walk to Noe Valley as well. I like the big cities for their diversity in people, energetic airports and mass transit, unique architecture, rooftop vista points, cafe culture, and how could I forget the variety of nomz.  I don't care much for main street shopping or gridlock traffic.

I equally like the unbeaten path for the sense of adventure, learning the local way of life, being able to see more than 10 stars at night, and loving the fact that I'm a little blue dot in the middle of nowhere on G00gle maps.  I'm not a fan of mozzies or sunblock eye sting.

Besides traveling and eating the world, I keep an active lifestyle of hitting the gym and playing tennis and volleyball.  But please don't ask me to do any distance running.

:-) :-)

The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. neighborhood_overview: The Mission is a diverse and vibrant neighborhood. This section, known as the Valencia Corridor, is home to the famous Dolores Park (just 1.5 blocks away) and Mission Dolores, as well as many hot eateries such as Tartine Bakery, Pizzeria Delfina, Craftsman & Wolves, Mission Cheese, and Dandelion Chocolate, to name a few.  The neighborhood retains some of its Latino past with many taquerias nearby, such as Taqueria Cancun just down the street, and a mural of native son Santana on the walk over.  The neighborhood features many such murals around every corner, including the wall that my building faces.  I recommend taking a walking tour to learn more about their history.
notes: My building was built in 1908, just two years after the big earthquake, and retains much of its original character, including redwood floors, a claw foot tub, wainscoting, and plate rails.  As an old building with lathe and plaster walls, this means you may also hear some noise from the neighbors including creaking floor boards, and you may occasionally hear some pitter patter from the dog living above.  The living room in the back is quite serene and overlooks the garden and a 100+ year old redwood tree (go ahead and hug it!).  The bedrooms face the street which is a dead end and usually very quiet, but remember this is urban living, so if you’re not accustomed to occasional street noise when you sleep, I’ve provided ear plugs and a sound machine which should do the trick.  I’ve enjoyed living in this flat for the past 12+ years and taking advantage of this exciting neighborhood and you are sure to love it too!

Located across from Airbnb HQ in an Airbnb Friendly Building, my apartment is at the intersection of Soma, the Mission, and Potrero Hill.  The perfect home base for any SF adventure.
space: Laid out in an open floor plan, my apartment offers everything you need for a comfortable stay.  The fully equipped kitchen sports new stainless steel appliances (including a large dishwasher, stove, fridge, and microwave) and plenty of dishes, glasses of all sorts, and silverware.  An enormous washer and dryer (with detergent provided) allows you to pack less.  The living room's big screen TV comes with Netflix, Hulu, HBO Go, and other streaming channels, as well as a Blu-ray player.  Its orange CB2 couch easily folds down into a roughly queen-size bed.  The bedroom has a king-sized memory-foam bed with a large closet.  Linens, towels, and toiletries all are provided.  And, best of all, central heat and air conditioning! Please note that this is a pet-friendly apartment.  I live here with my cat normally, but the cat won’t be there during your stay.

The sunset has plenty of charming restaurants, cafes, and nightlife. Best of all, it's a quiet and peaceful place to sleep without the noise and business of downtown!

We also have a parking space that you can arrange to use in advance.
access: Guests have full access to the ground floor of our home, which includes a shared bathroom, kitchenette, common space, and our garage with a washer and dryer. Tammy's room is downstairs, and the other 3 of us live separately upstairs.
interaction: We are sociable people who enjoy hosting and meeting visitors to the lovely city of San Francisco. We will mostly be working during your stay, but on our days off we love spending time with our guests at home or out in the city if it works for you! Of course, we also respect guests who prefer space and privacy. You can always reach us through the app, though during our work hours we may not be able to respond immediately.
house_rules: As adults hosting adults we ask that every guest respects the others on the property and maintains a clean environment. Here are a few house rules we ask our guests to follow: Please do not wear shoes inside. Socks or slippers on the wood floors are okay. The Airbnb includes access to downstairs only. You have everything you need there. If we are hanging out upstairs we will invite you to join us. You can also come up if you need to speak with one of us. Please turn off lights that you are not using, and don’t leave any lights on when you leave the house. Run the bathroom fan while you are showering and for a few minutes afterward. It will keep the bathroom comfortable and clean. Write down which bed you are using on the dry-erase board in the guestroom and use that bed for your entire stay unless you speak to us directly about switching beds. Please hang your bath towel on the hook in the bedroom that is labeled with the same letter as your bed. The beds are labeled by letters A - D.

neighborhood_overview: Golden Gate Heights is truly a unique neighborhood within the Sunset District of San Francisco.  Mostly residential and pretty quiet, you'll find nice little parks and some nice, steep walking. On the north end of Golden Gate Heights, check out Grand View Park, and on the southern end, Sunset Heights Park. A quick walk from the front door brings you to Hawk Hill Park, and just a few steps away is Larsen Peak and the aptly named Golden Gate Heights Park, a nice place to get in a game of tennis or visit the playground. Bordering neighborhoods provide all the restaurants and shopping you could ask for, while this is a nice neighborhood retreat.

Fair warning though, we are at the very top of a hill (hence the beautiful views!) so if you walk, the walk back isn't for the faint of heart.

neighborhood_overview: We are located in the heart of Telegraph Hill, a quintessential San Francisco neighborhood. Perhaps most famous for its Coit Tower, Telegraph Hill rises steeply out of North Beach and descends dramatically down to the Embarcadero. Each day hundreds of tourists climb Coit Tower’s 200 steps to take in an awe-inspiring 360-degree view of San Francisco and the greater Bay Area. Telegraph Hill is famous for the Filbert Street Steps - a beautiful pedestrian walkway that extends from Coit Tower down to Kearney Street at the edge of The Embarcadero. The Filbert steps leads walkers along a secluded path alongside charming gardens that belong to Telegraph Hill residents. The steps provide a great opportunity to catch a glimpse of the famous Telegraph Hill parrots. These beautiful bright green tropical birds are members of a greater colony of feral parrots that live at various locations throughout San Francisco.
notes: This accommodation is suitable for maximum two adults and a child under 12.
transit: The best way to explore is by foot. We are a block and a half west to Coit Tower and are within 20 minutes walking distance away from so many San Francisco attractions, Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39, Coit Tower, Lombard Street, Chinatown, Financial District, and etc. Using Car Share app such as Uber and Lyft is another popular way to get around San Francisco. The fare is usually under $10 if you ride within the city limit. For public transit, the No. 39 bus, half a block from our house, is pretty much the only choice. It winds its way up Telegraph Hill Boulevard to Coit Tower and down to Columbus and Broadway for connections to buses going to Union Square and the Financial District, or to Beach Street, for connections with the F streetcar, which runs along the Embarcadero.

neighborhood_overview: Named for Mission Dolores founded in 1776, San Francisco’s oldest neighborhood has some of its hottest new restaurants and galleries. Boasting some of the best weather in the city, the Mission District allows you to take advantage of an abundance of fog-free days. New restaurants and night spots are a draw while Mission Dolores, 16th and Dolores streets, is the oldest structure in San Francisco. Many of the city’s pioneers are buried in an adjacent cemetery. neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. neighborhood_overview: The property is conveniently located off the Third Street commercial corridor in the revitalized Bayview neighborhood, officially crowned as San Francisco Neighborhood of the Year in the 2015 Curbed Cup. There is an eclectic array of corner stores, restaurants, locally owned retail shoppes and boutiques, and cafes: Roadhouse Coffee Shop, Craftsmen & Wolves, Butchertown Gourmet, and Ritual Coffee. Proximal restaurants and bars include Sam Jordan's, The Jazz Club, Laughing Monk Brewery, 7 Stills, Flora Grubb, All Good Pizza, Yvonne Sweets, Harmonic Brewing, and much more. Our location is also ideal for those adventuring through the city by ride sharing, as Uber and Lyft are readily available with easy freeway access to 280 and 101 - SFO less than 15 minutes away. Limebike is also an option for those that prefer a two-wheeled experience. Look into CityPASS passports or downloading the MuniMobile app. There is a free street parking. However, parking can be challenging at times. Also, parking near or at tourist locations can be very expensive. If you’re coming from SFO, Über is probably your easiest and cheapest option at around $25.

neighborhood_overview: The Outer Mission, adjacent to the Excelsior and near the Balboa Park BART station, is considered one of the last working class neighborhoods of San Francisco. Mission Street in this part of town is the way Mission Street used to be: filled with taquerias and little Asian restaurants, produce markets and nail salons. There's a uniquely charming park about a five minute walk away from our home, where the gardener created sculptures out of fallen wood. McClaren Park, the 3rd largest park in San Francisco, is also within walking distance, and has miles of hiking trails, tennis courts and soccer fields. San Francisco City College is nearby, and San Francisco State University is a short drive or bus ride away.
notes: The in-law apartment is at the ground level, so there is some natural light but not a huge amount. The ceilings are not high, but my 6'1" son doesn't have a problem. It runs cool in the winter months, but there are several space heaters.
transit: There's a ton of public transportation, with the BART station a half mile away, and multiple buses on Mission Street even closer. You can be downtown in half an hour door to door. It's also right off 280 so easy to get to the Peninsula and the East Bay (if there's no traffic).
access: Guests have the living, kitchen, bedroom, and private bath area downstairs, and may use the garden as well.
interaction: We're happy to make suggestions for what to see in the city, and day trips to places like Point Reyes or Santa Cruz. We can also recommend our favorite bookstores, burrito places, and parks. When you arrive, you'll find an info sheet with the wifi password and a few neighborhood recommendations. If you let us know in advance, we'd be happy to also supply you with decaf coffee, if you prefer, and milk.

Since we live in eco-conscious San Francisco, we ask that guests follow compost, recycling and landfill guidelines. No candles.

neighborhood_overview: The Outer Sunset offers some of the best natural beauty that San Francisco has to offer, and it's away from the bustle of downtown. The salty ocean mist (only 5 blocks away) makes the sunset views even more spectacular on clear evenings. Our home is only 2 blocks from Golden Gate Park and a block away from the bustling shops and restaurants on Judah Street, giving you plenty of options within minutes walking distance.
notes: We've tried to make our house as "smart" as possible, including a Nest (to control the central heating) along with Dyson Hot+Cold fans in each of the bedrooms to make sure our guests are comfortable both on cool nights as well as during the Indian summers we experience in spring and fall. You could also take it a few more stops down to the Embarcadero to catch stunning views of the Bay Bridge. From the Embarcadero, there are also a few MUNI bus lines that can take you to Coit Tower and Fisherman's Wharf! That being said, Uber/Lyft are also extremely cheap and reliable, often times equal to the price of taking public transit (depending on the number of people communing) considering one-way on public transit is $2.75/person. In addition because of where the house sits on the block we have a very unusually large back yard that is perfect for lounging and playing.

neighborhood_overview: Noe Valley is an incredibly family friendly neighborhood whose bistros, coffee shops, and bookstores are always lively. The variety of shops allow you to buy anything from handmade Guatemalan textile products to Eileen Fisher ensembles.  There are many delectable restaurants that offer a broad range of food choices.  To really absorb the neighborhood, we suggest grabbing a wonderful coffee at Martha and Bros., a sumptuous scone from Noe Valley Bakery, and a piece of sunny sidewalk! We are close to small playgrounds and parks, and only a 15 minute walk to Dolores park.  In addition to the multiple city transportation options, there is a Ford GoBike station located a block from our home.

To pan your trip on public transit we use the website " (Website hidden by Airbnb)  There is also a great app we use called "NextBus-official" that geolocates where you are and then tells you which bus is coming when based on your location. neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. neighborhood_overview: Bayview is the sunniest part of San Francisco. It's a transitioning neighborhood, with a diverse population and lots of working and middle-class families. Folks are welcoming and friendly. There are some good restaurants nearby and traffic tends to be much lighter than other parts of the city. Free parking is almost always available on my block.

I have 2 dogs! Bayview district is not a fancy or expensive neighborhood, although house prices are right in line with San Francisco's famously pricey real estate market! neighborhood_overview: Safe, friendly, quiet.  If you love parks, beaches, restaurants, cafes, museums, open space and convenience, you'll love our neighborhood.  There's even a nearby Visitors Center and an historic, independent art-deco movie theater.  San Francisco weather is often mild, but it can get cold and foggy, especially during summer months;  when that happens, you'll want to dress warm.
notes: Please note that we live upstairs (so you may sometimes hear footsteps and/or other faint sounds from above). Please also note that there is no landline on the premises, so you will need a cell phone to make calls. San Francisco weather is often lovely, but it can get cold and foggy, especially in summer;  when this happens, you'll want to dress warm and you might hear foghorns.  We recommend bringing layers of clothing so you'll be prepared for all kinds of weather, as it can change from day to day and even within the same day.
transit: From our place it's easy to walk to Golden Gate Park, museums (The Legion of Honor is a 20 minute walk, the de Young and the Academy of Sciences are a 30 minute walk), the beach, Balboa Street (our local "downtown" area with restaurants/cafes/movie theater).  There are also several close bus lines (the 5 Fulton, 31 Balboa, 38 Geary and 1 California) which get you directly downtown or elsewhere.  Rent a bike or a Segway.  And of course, there are an abundance of Uber and Lyft drivers.  There's typically plenty of street parking, although when there's an event in the neighborhood, it can get more restricted.

host_about: Hi!  We are Tim and Lisa. We met while teaching at the well-respected preschool that Tim co-founded in 1984.  Tim comes from a hotel/restaurant family (The Treadway Inns in New England), and now newly retired, he looks forward to returning to his family roots as a friendly and helpful host.  Tim loves to garden and cook. Lisa still happily teaches 2-, 3- and 4-year-olds (coming up on her 30th year at the same school).  Like Tim, she is also from the East Coast (NY).  We put tons of love, care, comfort and quality into building our new apartment, as we expect to live down there ourselves one day.  We currently live upstairs from the apartment and are therefore easy to contact if you need anything (our guests choose how much or little interaction to have with us).  Please let us know if you have any questions!

name: Brand New! Chic studio with downtown view
summary: This spacious and bright studio has a private entry, kitchenette, hardwood floors, beautiful spotless bathroom, a comfortable queen bed with memory foam & quality linens and a futon love seat that folds out to a small bed, low on the floor. There is a private deck and yard. It is a lovely place to relax, with a view over the Mission of downtown. There is a smart TV.  Nearby are cozy cafes, unique restaurants, a park and playground and public transportation. There is easy access to the freeway.
space: This bright and roomy studio is a comfortable space with a large north-facing glass wall with a view of downtown.  The studio is on the ground floor of our house, but there are 2 steps down from the hallway to the main room of the studio. Because we live on a hill, even the ground floor has a fabulous view. There is a comfortable queen size bed with a memory foam mattress topper, night stands and reading lights.  There is a dining table with 4 chairs.  A sitting area has a love seat and an oversize armchair.  The love seat folds out into a bed for a third guest.  We can also bring in a rollaway bed.  There is a large-screen TV with local channels and Netflix, or you can stream your own movies or online channels.  There is a armoire and dresser drawers for your use. We provide coffee and tea for you

neighborhood_overview: The studio is in Bernal Heights.  It is on the North slope, and our home has a view over the Mission district and to Downtown. Bernal Heights is hilly, with great views, some steep streets, stairways and tiny parks tucked into side streets. From the park at the top of our hill, about 3 blocks away, there is a 360-degree view of the City, including the bay, the Bay Bridge, the Golden Gate bridge, Twin Peaks, Downtown, Mt Diablo and south to the airport. During baseball season and at the 4th of July, fireworks are often visible from our hill. There is another very sweet local park about 2 blocks away, perfect for kids, dogs and just strolling.  There are several cafes and restaurants around the park.  There is a lovely small market at the other end of the park, perfect for stocking up for a picnic. notes: There are no laundry facilities. A laundromat is a few blocks away. Pets are permissible, but may not be left alone in the studio. Please clean up after your pet if you let them in the yard. Please don't use "puppy pads" in the studio. No one under 18 will be allowed to stay without an adult. Our studio is not appropriate for parties or events. There is no smoking inside the studio, however we do allow smoking outside on the deck or in the backyard. We will charge a $200 fee if you have smoked in the studio. Licensed in San Francisco
transit: It is about 2 blocks to a bus stop, a little less than 1 mile to a BART station. Buses and BART run all night. You can also take either a bus or BART train to connect to CalTrain to get down to Silicon Valley, Stanford or San Jose. You can get to and from the SFO or OAK airport on BART. Mission St, Valencia St and 24th St (Calle 24 Latino Cultural District) in the Mission neighborhood are walking distance. Cortland Avenue, our quaint neighborhood commercial district is a few hilly blocks away as well. Essential services like laundry, groceries, coffee, restaurants, ice cream and several parks are within a couple of blocks. A determined pedestrian could easily walk to Noe Valley as well. Our home is about halfway up a hill from the flats of Precita Park and Cesar Chavez St. If you have a car, there is very quick and easy access to I-280, I-80 and I-101 for access to the South Bay and San Jose, to Oakland and Berkeley in the East Bay and to Downtown. You will be able to lock the studio when you are here and take the key with you when you are out for the day. If you want to come earlier, you can check with us and if its possible we'll be able to let you in early. At the very least, you can almost certainly drop by early and leave your bags until the studio is ready for check in. The deck off the studio has a stair down to the yard, and you are free to go in our urban backyard.

Benefiting from Twin Peaks blocking the strong winds and fog almost year-round, Dolores Heights remains relatively warm, sunny and fog-free. Exploring the steep stairs and streets by foot is a favorite pastime of residents and visitors alike and we provide a walking-tour map.
notes: For the safety and security of all who occupy the Suite, the House and the Cottage, entrances and yards are monitored and recorded by motion and audio activated video cameras. The neighborhood is quiet and secluded. We cannot host any guests who are loud, play loud music, or invite other people into our homes for drinking or just hanging out.
transit: The "J" street car stop is a 1 block walk to a station at Dolores Park. Its connects to many buses along the route to downtown as well as various lines of the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) system which travel to the East and South Bay communities and the San Francisco and Oakland airports. There are numerous bus lines within two blocks of the Suite which connect to all parts of the City and its various attractions. Overnight and weekend parking is unlimited, but for those without a permit parking it is limited to two hours between 8 am and 9 pm. My experience is that parked cars on our secluded and remote street are seldom monitored for time restrictions except on Wednesday... street cleaning day. The dining and shopping areas of the Castro, Dolores Park, and Noe Valley are short downhill walks from the Suite. If you are challenged with uphill walking we suggest you return by Lyft or Uber which are ubiquitous.
interaction: Since we live on the property we are close by and always available by phone. As a native San Franciscan I love to answer questions and make recommendations about the City, but I'm happy to respect your privacy.

neighborhood_overview: Located directly south of the Mission District, Bernal Heights is a quiet residential neighborhood with plenty of green space and a wide range of shops and eateries along picturesque Cortland Avenue. From the apartment, you can take a brisk one-mile trek to the summit of Bernal Hill, a favorite spot for local picnickers that offers expansive views of the Financial District to the north, Twin Peaks to the west, and Glen Park to the south. My home is located at the base of Bernal Hill. This  small  valley is  called Precita Valley, surrounded on three sides by hills, Precita Valley itself is relatively flat. Precita Park is 65 feet from the door and boasts a Cafe at either end. A  walk up the hill under Folsom Street’s tree canopy will take you to the top with the 360 degree views and plenty of hiking paths. You can also opt for a shorter (and less hilly) walk to 24th Street in San Francisco’s fast-evolving Mission District, where new restaurants rub elbows with tried-and-true taquerias.

neighborhood_overview: We are centrally located in the heart of SF.  Alamo Square / Hayes Valley is one of the most vibrant and revitalized neighborhoods in San Francisco. It includes wine bars, cafes, five-star restaurants, high-end boutiques, clubs, bars, close to movie theaters, Civic Center/City Hall, Asian Art Museum, the symphony & the Opera House and much more.  Public transportation is very convenient with a bus line right across the street if you want to head downtown (21 Hayes) or to the beach. The 5 Fulton line is just 2 blocks away.   You can find some of the best coffee and foods in this part of the city and much more in the nearby districts.  Also within 1 mile walking distance is the Fillmore District which offers the same with a handful of jazz clubs to enjoy.  You have the Painted Ladies to the right and City Hall to the left, Western Addition behind you and the Lower Haight in front of you.  Great spot to be!
notes: You will CLIMB STAIRS to the top - 3rd floor!  This building still has the original staircase from the 1900's. The spiral staircase was removed so you can get through with your suitcases!  We have a small water heater so it's best to take short, quick showers in order to have enough hot water to go around for a large group...especially since we are experiencing a drought/water shortage in CA.  At present, the hot tub cannot be offered as an amenity at this time.  If you want to use it during your stay, please contact the owner to make prior arrangements.  The main closet is partly occupied by the owner's personal belongings.  Half the closet is available for you to use or hang your clothes on the suit rack provided in addition to the rack in the second bedroom.  There will be an additional fee for laundry service if you want more towels other than what is provided and/or linen service.  Please be considerate of our water shortage/drought in CA.
transit: BY BUS: I suggest to use public transportation.  The 21 HAYES is right outside of our apartment!  This convenient bus line will take you directly downtown and connects onto other bus lines that will bring you to other neighborhoods throughout the city.  Another bus line close by is the 5 FULTON which is only 2 blocks south of us (behind the apt).  It's only a 10 minute walk to Van Ness MUNI station, and 15 minute walk to Civic Center MUNI station for BART and other MUNI lines.   MUNI is an integral part of public transit in our city, operating year round and connecting with regional transportation services, such as BART, Caltrain, SamTrans, and AC Transit.   ADULT FARE:  $2.25 CHILDREN:  $.75c  (ages 5 - 17yrs) The city's lone subway tube is called MUNI Metro; also 3 cable car lines, and a heritage streetcar line known as the F Market & Wharves.  MUNI shares 4 metro stations with BART. Travelers can connect onto San Francisco & Oakland International Airports via BART.  BY CAR: Convenie

neighborhood_overview: The Mission District's multifarious corridors comprise an inviting and colorful melting pot of cultures, cuisines, and scenes. Named for Mission Dolores founded in 1776, San Francisco’s oldest and historically Latino neighborhood has some of its hottest new restaurants and galleries and boasts some of the best weather in the city (read: the sunny side of the city!).  New restaurants and night spots are a draw while Mission Dolores, at 16th and Dolores street, is the oldest structure in San Francisco. Many of the city’s pioneers are buried in an adjacent cemetery. The largest concentration of murals in the city adorn buildings, fences and walls throughout the district.

It’s perfectly fine if you want to relax in the evening and watch a movie, it’s just not ideal to hang out in for prolonged periods of time. If you are traveling solo and/or will be out and about for most of the time, it’s very well suited for that type of stay.  3. The vast majority of couples who have stayed here had no complaints but a handful have since they didn’t notice the detail ahead of time in the listing. It's a centrally located, vibrant neighborhood - an area of tree-lined residential streets intersected by a lively boulevard lined with cafes, eclectic store fronts and some of the city's most popular bars & restaurants. We have great food and great fun on all sides! The rhythm of the Beat poets flow in the streets outside their regular hangouts, like Vesuvio, and City Lights Bookstore, just a couple of blocks away. host_about:
There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. At first glance, one might presume that the endgame of all hostels is to create a sense of firm familiarity among guest and staff alike, but with us, you can feel it. With a full roster of events that are ongoing, all inclusive in both experience and price, and a design purposefully conducive to the gathering of folks all around the world, we are dedicated to establishing a world reaching community that you feel while you are here, and long after your stay.

Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

neighborhood_overview: The Sunset is our favorite neighborhood in San Francisco! We are close to Golden Gate Park, Golden Gate Bridge, Lands End, Twin Peaks and Ocean Beach. In Golden Gate Park you can visit the de Young Museum of art, The Japanese Tea Garden, the Conservatory of Flowers, the Botanical Garden, and the Academy of Sciences. The sunset has plenty of charming restaurants, cafes, and nightlife. Best of all, it's a quiet and peaceful place to sleep without the noise and business of downtown!
notes: We are flexible with check-in and check-out times, so feel free to let us know your situation in advance. We will do our best to accommodate your arrival or departure needs! We have key-less access to the house, so you can check-in even if we aren't at home. Your bed may not be prepared by the time you arrive, but we will have it ready by the evening before you sleep. This is because we go to work before check-out time and don't return home until the evening. Feel free to arrive in the afternoon or late morning to drop off your luggage.
transit: There are several Muni bus and train lines within a couple blocks of our place that run 24-hours and can get you anywhere in the city. The N-Judah, L-Taraval, 28, and 7 are the main options. We all commute daily to SoMa, The Marina, and Financial District. Public transit is very easy to use in San Francisco, and of course we will be available to help you! We also have a parking space that you can arrange to use in advance.
access: Guests have full access to the ground floor of our home, which includes a shared bathroom, kitchenette, common space, and our garage with a washer and dryer. Tammy's room is downstairs, and the other 3 of us live separately upstairs.
interaction: We are sociable people who enjoy hosting and meeting visitors to the lovely city of San Francisco. We will mostly be working during your stay, but on our days off we love spending time with our guests at home or out in the city if it works for you! Of course, we also respect guests who prefer space and privacy. You can always reach us through the app, though during our work hours we may not be able to respond immediately.
house_rules: As adults hosting adults we ask that every guest respects the others on the property and maintains a clean environment. Here are a few house rules we ask our guests to follow: Please do not wear shoes inside. Socks or slippers on the wood floors are okay. The Airbnb includes access to downstairs only. You have everything you need there. If we are hanging out upstairs we will invite you to join us. You can also come up if you need to speak with one of us. Please turn off lights that you are not using, and don’t leave any lights on when you leave the house. Run the bathroom fan while you are showering and for a few minutes afterward. It will keep the bathroom comfortable and clean. Write down which bed you are using on the dry-erase board in the guestroom and use that bed for your entire stay unless you speak to us directly about switching beds. Please hang your bath towel on the hook in the bedroom that is labeled with the same letter as your bed. The beds are labeled by letters A - D.

transit: San Francisco is more of a walking city than a driving city. Because of that, parking can be very expensive. However, CalTrain and Bart (Bay Area Rapid Transit) will help.  Muni trains and buses run throughout the area, and cabs are easily hailed. Uber also serves this area as well as the rest of San Francisco. Caltrain provides commuter rail service along the San Francisco Peninsula, through the South Bay to San Jose and Gilroy.  Caltrain is a proof-of-purchase system. Passengers must have a valid ticket before boarding the train and must show their ticket to a conductor or fare inspector upon request. Those without a valid ticket may be cited and fined. Tickets aren't sold on the train. Stations are equipped with ticket machines, and most stations offer both parking and bicycle access.  *This information is deemed reliable but not guaranteed.

host_about:
We have been providing vacation rental apartments for over 10 years across the East Coast. We are known for our distinctively furnished apartments in popular locations, and for our attentive service. You’ll find that our rates are quite reasonable. If you're looking for a safe, comfortable place with fabulous amenities and Wi-Fi (we know you need the Wi-Fi!) in the Boston MA area, Washington DC, Miami FL or very close to NYC in Jersey City or Hoboken, we'd love to host you. Many of the buildings where our apartments are located feature amenities such as beautiful lobbies, 24 hour front desk staff, fitness centers, business centers, recreation rooms, indoor or outdoor pools and whirlpools. If you are traveling with children, some buildings offer playgrounds (many buildings are near public playgrounds as well) or indoor playrooms. Depending on the location, you can stay for just a few days, a week, a month or more. 

We offer an assortment of short-term apartments in sizes ranging from a studio to three bedrooms that are fully furnished with all the comforts of home. Our local staff meticulously prepares your apartment before your arrival, and we offer 24 hour assistance for any emergencies after business hours. When you arrive at your apartment, the beds will be made, towels and bath amenities will be stocked in the bathrooms, and the coffee maker will be set up in the kitchen with some sample coffees, sweetener and creamer (teabags too if that is your preference) to start your morning off properly. If you’d like to cook a meal, the kitchen is stocked with dishes, cutlery, glassware and pots and pans. The living room is set up with a TV and cable channels, and the Wi-Fi router password and instructions will be prominently displayed so you can get connected quickly. You can also make local and toll-free phone calls at no charge. 

Please contact us to confirm the exact availability of the apartment you are interested in. We’d love to host you (and your family) for your vacation or business trip.

name: Charming Family Home in San Francisco
summary: Welcome to our kid-friendly home! This 110 year-old newly restored Edwardian is full of natural light, close to all types of public transportation (Muni (bus/rail), BART (subway)), and is surrounded by authentic bodegas and restaurants. At the foot of SF's second largest park, McLaren Park, we are also within 1 block of two different playgrounds. Also within 4 mins of both 101 and 280 highways, making travel easy, parking included! Has 2 queen-beds + a twin bed, great for couples and families!
space: With original hardwood floors and an arched ceiling in the living room, this home is quintessential San Francisco. The living room sports bay windows, and has a desk + external monitor, HD television, Apple TV, and two couches. One couch rolls out into a very comfortable slat-supported queen bed (no uncomfortable springs or metal wires). Our son's room has a twin bed, with tons of toys and books to play with. The dining room table can fit six, and also has a small keyboard if someone wants to be serenaded. The kitchen is huge for SF standards, with all new stainless steel appliances, including a 5-burner gas range. A large hallway contains a second desk, laser printer and new high-efficiency washer and dryer. The master bedroom has a queen bed and bay window, looking out onto the Glen Park hills and our neighbor's palm trees.

notes: Wifi + Netflix + Hulu + Apple TV included. Our home has in-floor radiant heating, with four different Nest-E thermostats, so everyone can adjust the temperature to their own comfort level in each room as they sleep. If you are staying in the city, you might also consider taking Lyft or Uber, which can get you almost anywhere in SF in under 15 mins from our home for under $20 (does not include peak traffic times). There is a Mollie Stones market 5 blocks away, and a Safeway and Whole Foods are a 15 minute walk (or 1 MUNI stop).  I love how much the Castro is a neighborhood, with it's own distinct character. neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood is called Noe Valley. This peaceful and friendly neighborhood puts you in an idealic place where you gain some peace and quiet away from the hustle of the main city- while still being a short distance from downtown. Twin Peaks is nearby for some incredible views, and Dolores Park is a nice 5 minute walk for some weekend fun and relaxation. 24th street offers all the shops, salons, coffee houses (we recommend La Boulangerie!) and restaurants you can enjoy. Finally, Whole Foods is a quick 3 minute walk for your grocery shopping.

transit: The house is conveniently located 2 blocks away from the MUNI J line. This train comes every 12 minutes, and takes you to the center of the city (Market st) in less than 10 minutes or Financial District in about 20!  The 24th st and Mission BART station are 5 blocks away for easy access to the the entire Bay Area.  Also, if you’re a biker, we offer secured storage in our garage.  Besides all of these, the city is equipped with multiple gig economy businesses to get you around town. Lyft and Uber are prevalent and offer rides to anywhere you need to go within minutes, Scoot offers motor bike rentals for $3 = 30 minutes, which is enough to take you anywhere in the city. Bird, Spin and Lime offer a brand new option to grab a standup scooter to ride starting at $1. Ford Go bikes and JUMP are the best bike share companies if you don’t want to worry about bringing or purchasing your own bike. host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

neighborhood_overview: Clarendon Heights is a charming terraced neighborhood just North of Twin Peaks, with winding narrow streets, unique architecture from the late 1800's, early 1900's, mid-century modern homes, and storybook stairways like the Pemberton Steps.  It sits above the Castro and Cole Valley and is walking distance to Golden Gate Park and Sutro Forest.  You can also hop over to Tank Hill Park, just a few few minutes away and see the Golden Gate Bridge, or head up to Twin Peaks for 360 degree views of San Francisco.  Stroll down the hill for a film at the historic Castro Theatre, or for brunch at the famed Zazie in Cole Valley.

host_about:
I grew up in New York and have been living in San Francisco for the past 16 years.  I sometimes spend summers and winters in Greece and Cyprus, visiting extended family and  friends across the Mediterranean.  

I have had the good fortune of meeting and being hosted by extraordinary people.  I met one of my closest and dearest friends while sitting in a Cafe in Firenze - she showed me around the city and invited me to stay in her home when I visited a few months later.  I love being able to share my home and experience of San Francisco.  

One of my favorite ways to spend a morning is walking at Ocean Beach with the shore birds as the sun is rising.  I also love seeing films, listening to live music, being  with friends, reading, relaxing, and being around beauty.  I'm very partial to warm days.

When I'm traveling I'm usually visiting people I know and love learning new neighborhoods, finding local markets and shops, and eating local food.  

I like living in and creating a peaceful and easy atmosphere for people, with lots of light, warmth and beauty.  I've hosted lots of wonderful people in my home; some have written books here, composed music, and others have just enjoyed a place to retreat in SF.

neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood is called Noe Valley. This peaceful and friendly neighborhood puts you in an idealic place where you gain some peace and quiet away from the hustle of the main city- while still being a short distance from downtown. Twin Peaks is nearby for some incredible views, and Dolores Park is a nice 5 minute walk for some weekend fun and relaxation. 24th street offers all the shops, salons, coffee houses (we recommend La Boulangerie!) and restaurants you can enjoy. Finally, Whole Foods is a quick 3 minute walk for your grocery shopping.
notes: With over 60 rooms in the San Francisco Bay area, our "Ben|n|Build Community" is large enough in size and diversity for us to organize monthly events. All our members are invited to attend, mingle and expand their network - while enjoying refreshments and food.
transit: The house is conveniently located 2 blocks away from the MUNI J line. This train comes every 12 minutes, and takes you to the center of the city (Market st) in less than 10 minutes or Financial District in about 20!  The 24th st and Mission BART station are 5 blocks away for easy access to the the entire Bay Area.  Also, if you’re a biker, we offer secured storage in our garage.  Besides all of these, the city is equipped with multiple gig economy businesses to get you around town. Lyft and Uber are prevalent and offer rides to anywhere you need to go within minutes, Scoot offers motor bike rentals for $3 = 30 minutes, which is enough to take you anywhere in the city. Bird, Spin and Lime offer a brand new option to grab a standup scooter to ride starting at $1. Ford Go bikes and JUMP are the best bike share companies if you don’t want to worry about bringing or purchasing your own bike. Utilizing these great options will keep you out of traffic and getting to where you want to be.
access: All guests enjoy full access to the kitchen and living room a.k.a. Communal Spaces. In addition we have a small library and a washer and dryer for complimentary use. The whole place has a total of 2 full bathrooms for everyone to use + 2 private bathrooms for those guests who decide to have an upgrade and have a bathroom on their own room. All of these bathrooms are newly remodeled and with a shower over a tub.
interaction: Once the booking is complete, our Community Manager will reach out to you, coordinate your check-in, and answer any question you might have about the house, the city, or our amazing Community. Feel free to email, text, call or slack any member of our team if there is anything you need. Contacts information will be provided upon check-in.

host_about:
Welcome to Bed|n|Build! 

Bed|n|Build provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world.

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house with you, or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

neighborhood_overview: Dolores Heights is centrally located between the Castro, Noe Valley and the Mission. It includes Mission Dolores -- the oldest building in San Francisco, and Dolores Park -- one of the most popular parks in the city. As you may know, the Castro (centered 4 blocks west) is the historic gay center of San Francisco -- it features restaurants, bars, the Castro Theater, shopping, and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and day spas. The Mission (centered 3 blocks east) is a historically Latino neighborhood. It, too, features restaurants, bars, the Roxie Theater, shopping and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and boutiques.

The Muni J-Church line is two blocks away and will take you downtown; it also connects with other lines that can take you to virtually any part of SF. The Castro and Church stations are four blocks away. The 22, 24, 33, and F all stop within 2-4 blocks of the apartment and will take you to various parts of the city. BART is also nearby -- the 16th & Mission station is only five blocks away. There is a bike share station 18th and Dolores street 3 blocks away. In fact, everything you need is easily walkable, so you don't need a car. If you do have a car, free on-street parking is available. Parking spots are typically ample, and with notice you can use the private spot in front of the driveway. neighborhood_overview: Dolores Heights is centrally located between the Castro, Noe Valley and the Mission. It includes Mission Dolores -- the oldest building in San Francisco, and Dolores Park -- one of the most popular parks in the city. As you may know, the Castro (centered 4 blocks west) is the historic gay center of San Francisco -- it features restaurants, bars, the Castro Theater, shopping, and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and day spas. The Mission (centered 3 blocks east) is a historically Latino neighborhood. It, too, features restaurants, bars, the Roxie Theater, shopping and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and boutiques.

For your information: there is an apartment above the home; you may intersect with the neighbors living above in the stairs area. The neighbors are respectful and quiet. The unit is mostly soundproof, but you may occasionally hear people walking upstairs (as is usually the case in apartments)
transit: San Francisco has excellent public transportation, and all of it is easily accessible from here. The Muni J-Church line is two blocks away and will take you downtown; it also connects with other lines that can take you to virtually any part of SF. The Castro and Church stations are four blocks away. The 22, 24, 33, and F all stop within 2-4 blocks of the apartment and will take you to various parts of the city. BART is also nearby -- the 16th & Mission station is only five blocks away. There is a bike share station 18th and Dolores street 3 blocks away. In fact, everything you need is easily walkable, so you don't need a car. If you do have a car, free on-street parking is available.
