I grew up in New York and have been living in San Francisco for the past 16 years.  I sometimes spend summers and winters in Greece and Cyprus, visiting extended family and  friends across the Mediterranean.  

I have had the good fortune of meeting and being hosted by extraordinary people.  I met one of my closest and dearest friends while sitting in a Cafe in Firenze - she showed me around the city and invited me to stay in her home when I visited a few months later.  I love being able to share my home and experience of San Francisco.  

One of my favorite ways to spend a morning is walking at Ocean Beach with the shore birds as the sun is rising.  I also love seeing films, listening to live music, being  with friends, reading, relaxing, and being around beauty.  I'm very partial to warm days.

When I'm traveling I'm usually visiting people I know and love learning new neighborhoods, finding local markets and shops, and eating local food.  

I like living in and creating a peaceful and easy atmosphere for people, with lots of light, warmth and beauty.  I've hosted lots of wonderful people in my home; some have written books here, composed music, and others have just enjoyed a place to retreat in SF.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

We are close to 2 parks. The views are incredible - 360 views of the entire Bay Area as you stroll around Bernal Hill a block away. These are the "temporary" houses put up after the 1906 earthquake. Lots to love for sure. I’ve lived in San Francisco for 22 years now, prior to which I lived in Asia (Tokyo, Japan to be specific). I also consider myself a citizen of the world, as I have traveled to over 50 countries so far and in addition to English, speak some Japanese and French. 

In my travels, I have stayed at some amazing places and know what a difference great hospitality can make to a trip. I therefore strive to create an experience at Standout Stays that will be memorable and unique. My aim is that you will come back each time you return to San Francisco to stay here again. 

I know the city and surrounding area very well and am always happy to give suggestions to make your stay exceptional. I am also a foodie and am working on a type of food blog — so if you are looking for great restaurants, I can share with you my favorites.

As a guest, I am responsible, trustworthy, and neat. Being a host myself, I can completely put myself in your shoes and am very respectful of your space. I love AirBNB because it really affords one the opportunity to live like a local when you travel to a new area.

In my free time, I enjoy spending time with my dog (Dexter), working out, hiking, traveling, skiing, and generally making the most of life. 

If you are considering booking one of my listings, I know you will love your stay here!

If I have made a reservation request with you, I can promise that you will be delighted to have me as a guest.

Hope to meet you soon,

Laurence

Three blocks full of cute restaurants, a post office, library, park, a movie theatre, boutique shops and beauty salons. neighborhood_overview: Our house in the sunset is perfectly situated to access the entire city using public transportation or walking.  We're close to Inner Sunset and Irving area, Golden Gate Park, and Dim Sum (Irving Street) are walking distance from the house. Irving street is a bustling corridor of activity, especially weekends. There's so many good restaurants around the corner. Grab tasty Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese,  Pakistani, Japanese, Middle Eastern, Taiwanese Boba or go to the local and good grocery store round the corner and cook a meal at home. Fun thrift shopping and many Chinese versions of the "dollar store." It's a safe neighborhood to wander around. Easy access to both the Ocean Beach and Financial District/Downtown via the L Line Streetcar.
notes: We live upstairs and always try to soften our steps but you may hear us on occasion. Please let us know if it's ever too loud : ) We do have a Smart TV- you can stream Netflix, Hulu, etc. but no cable.
transit: The best way to get around SF is by foot! There's no better way to experience all sights and smells! Uber/Lyft are the quickest way to get across town. Both are incredibly reliable and inexpensive. We highly recommend this option and you can get Downtown for about $10. Public transit is always an option but will take much longer than Uber. Two blocks away there's a stop for the L  streetcar that'll take you directly to downtown within 30 minutes.  Rental cars aren't advised. Parking can be tricky in the city. It's often difficult to find a spot and once you do, the city aggressively enforces the parking regulations. Tickets start at $70 and getting towed starts at $500.  We do not offer a dedicated parking spot but it's a quiet street and parking is very easy to find!

You’ll be right around the corner from shops, coffee houses, restaurants, bars on Polk street, and grocery stores including Trader Joe’s and Whole Foods. Take a jog down to China town, or a walk over to Fisherman’s Wharf. A 15 minute bike ride puts you right in the Financial District for an easy commute to and from work. We love the Contraband coffee bar just 2 blocks over for a great atmosphere to work and sip your favorite pour over brew. Everything you need is easy to get to!
notes: With over 60 rooms in the San Francisco Bay area, our "Ben|n|Build Community" is large enough in size and diversity for us to organize monthly events. All our members are invited to attend, mingle and expand their network - while enjoying refreshments and food.
transit: The house is right around the corner from the MUNI Bus stop at Clay and Larkin, buses run roughly every 10 minutes. This route takes you directly into the FiDi area and will make your morning ride into the heart of downtown simple. If you’re a biker, we offer secured storage in our back yard.  Besides all of these, the city is equipped with multiple gig economy businesses to get you around town. Lyft and Uber are prevalent and offer rides to anywhere you need to go within minutes, Scoot offers motor bike rentals for $3 = 30 minutes, which is enough to take you anywhere in the city. Bird, Spin and Lime offer a brand new option to grab a standup scooter to ride starting at $1. Ford Go bikes and JUMP are the best bike share companies if you don’t want to worry about bringing or purchasing your own bike. Utilizing these great options will keep you out of traffic and getting to where you want to be.
access: All guests enjoy full access to the kitchen and living room a.k.a. Communal Spaces. In addition we have a small library and a washer and dryer for complimentary use. All bathrooms are newly remodeled.
interaction: Once the booking is complete, our Community Manager will reach out to you, coordinate your check-in, and answer any question you might have about the house, the city, or our amazing Community. Feel free to email, text, call or slack any member of our team if there is anything you need. Contacts information will be provided upon check-in.

host_about:
Welcome to Bed|n|Build! Bed|n|Build provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

We partner with startup accelerators, bootcamps, coding academies, and co-working spaces and prefer recruiting our residents through peer-recommendations and our networks. So please let us know how you have heard from us.

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

neighborhood_overview: Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. host_about: I first came to San Francisco in 2011 after years of traveling the world (mostly with Airbnb!) As both a host and a guest, I enjoy sharing stories and local tips with those I meet. Having lived in 9 countries and traveled to many more, I strive to be the sort of guest that can fit in anywhere and the sort of host that can make anyone feel at home. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. If you are considering booking one of my listings, I know you will love your stay here!

Hope to meet you soon,

Laurence

neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood is called Noe Valley. This peaceful and friendly neighborhood puts you in an idealic place where you gain some peace and quiet away from the hustle of the main city- while still being a short distance from downtown. Twin Peaks is nearby for some incredible views, and Dolores Park is a nice 5 minute walk for some weekend fun and relaxation. 24th street offers all the shops, salons, coffee houses (we recommend La Boulangerie!) and restaurants you can enjoy. Finally, Whole Foods is a quick 3 minute walk for your grocery shopping.
notes: With over 60 rooms in the San Francisco Bay area, our "Ben|n|Build Community" is large enough in size and diversity for us to organize monthly events. All our members are invited to attend, mingle and expand their network - while enjoying refreshments and food.
transit: The house is conveniently located 2 blocks away from the MUNI J line. This train comes every 12 minutes, and takes you to the center of the city (Market st) in less than 10 minutes or Financial District in about 20!  The 24th st and Mission BART station are 5 blocks away for easy access to the the entire Bay Area.  Also, if you’re a biker, we offer secured storage in our garage.  Besides all of these, the city is equipped with multiple gig economy businesses to get you around town. Lyft and Uber are prevalent and offer rides to anywhere you need to go within minutes, Scoot offers motor bike rentals for $3 = 30 minutes, which is enough to take you anywhere in the city. Bird, Spin and Lime offer a brand new option to grab a standup scooter to ride starting at $1. Ford Go bikes and JUMP are the best bike share companies if you don’t want to worry about bringing or purchasing your own bike. Utilizing these great options will keep you out of traffic and getting to where you want to be.
access: All guests enjoy full access to the kitchen and living room a.k.a. Communal Spaces. In addition we have a small library and a washer and dryer for complimentary use. The whole place has a total of 2 full bathrooms for everyone to use + 2 private bathrooms for those guests who decide to have an upgrade and have a bathroom on their own room. All of these bathrooms are newly remodeled and with a shower over a tub.
interaction: Once the booking is complete, our Community Manager will reach out to you, coordinate your check-in, and answer any question you might have about the house, the city, or our amazing Community. Feel free to email, text, call or slack any member of our team if there is anything you need. Contacts information will be provided upon check-in.

host_about:
Welcome to Bed|n|Build! 

Bed|n|Build provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world.

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house with you, or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. transit: San Francisco is more of a walking city than a driving city. Because of that, parking can be very expensive. However, Mission Bay and China Basin are both served by the city's excellent public transportation system. Muni trains and buses run throughout the area, and cabs are easily hailed. Uber also serves this area as well as the rest of San Francisco. Caltrain provides commuter rail service along the San Francisco Peninsula, through the South Bay to San Jose and Gilroy. We have been providing vacation rental apartments for over 10 years across the East Coast. We are known for our distinctively furnished apartments in popular locations, and for our attentive service. You’ll find that our rates are quite reasonable. If you're looking for a safe, comfortable place with fabulous amenities and Wi-Fi (we know you need the Wi-Fi!) in the Boston MA area, Washington DC, Miami FL or very close to NYC in Jersey City or Hoboken, we'd love to host you. Many of the buildings where our apartments are located feature amenities such as beautiful lobbies, 24 hour front desk staff, fitness centers, business centers, recreation rooms, indoor or outdoor pools and whirlpools. If you are traveling with children, some buildings offer playgrounds (many buildings are near public playgrounds as well) or indoor playrooms. Depending on the location, you can stay for just a few days, a week, a month or more. 

We offer an assortment of short-term apartments in sizes ranging from a studio to three bedrooms that are fully furnished with all the comforts of home. Our local staff meticulously prepares your apartment before your arrival, and we offer 24 hour assistance for any emergencies after business hours. When you arrive at your apartment, the beds will be made, towels and bath amenities will be stocked in the bathrooms, and the coffee maker will be set up in the kitchen with some sample coffees, sweetener and creamer (teabags too if that is your preference) to start your morning off properly. If you’d like to cook a meal, the kitchen is stocked with dishes, cutlery, glassware and pots and pans. The living room is set up with a TV and cable channels, and the Wi-Fi router password and instructions will be prominently displayed so you can get connected quickly. You can also make local and toll-free phone calls at no charge. 

Please contact us to confirm the exact availability of the apartment you are interested in. We’d love to host you (and your family) for your vacation or business trip.

neighborhood_overview: The Inner Richmond is one of the most popular, convenient neighborhoods in San Francisco:  - Three blocks from Golden Gate Park, specifically near The California Academy of Sciences, De Young Museum, Japanese Gardens, and Arboretum.  - Three blocks from Clement Street, including its fabulous restaurants (such as Burma Superstar, B Star, Troya, Giorgio’s Pizza, Toy Boat Dessert), many coffee shops, See’s Candies, bakeries, Green Apple Bookstore (regularly voted best used bookstore in SF), spas, and more  - The Inner Richmond is home to the “other” or “real” Chinatown (less touristy than downtown)  - Five blocks from the Presidio, where you can experience breath-taking views, hikes and golf  - Convenient grocery shopping, including Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s, 24-hour Safeway, fresh fruit markets, and many Asian supermarkets.  - Great location for running and biking (multiple bike rental shops nearby; secure bike storage is available in our garage).

We are 1 block away from the bus stop, and a 2min Taxi/Uber ride to the nearest BART/Muni station (Glen Park Station) so it's easy to visit the Ferry Building, Union Square, Downtown... Everywhere! In addition, the Farmer's Market is 1 block away from our home every weekend... so if you feel like doing some home cooking, this is the perfect chance! Then again, you might want to explore some places outside of SF! If that's the case, my home is conveniently located right off the 280 Freeway. Feeling like a quick trip to San Mateo to taste some of the best Japanese food in the Bay Area? You will skip ALL the city traffic and get there in less than 20minutes! Or if you're want to explore Silicon Valley and see what all the technology hype is all about, Palo Alto is a 40 minute drive.
notes: My home was newly built in 2004. So it's fairly new compared to 90% of the housing in SF. Most are ~100 years old!  There are 2 flights of stairs. While this makes for quick access to the freeways it also comes with a little noise. The windows are double glazed but a low hum of traffic can be heard from the front rooms. You don't notice it after a few minutes and it hasn't bothered anyone to date but I just want you to be aware. :) Pets are allowed depending on the size... smaller the better! You will need to keep him/her in your room at all times and clean up after him/her. If he/she leaves a mess, you will be charged extra for the cleaning fee.
transit: Free parking on our street (the chances of you not finding a parking spot is slim)!! This is something SF lacks... A LOT. Or If you prefer, I also have 1 spot in the parking garage, which I would be happy to lend to you for a small fee.

neighborhood_overview: Dolores Heights is centrally located between the Castro, Noe Valley and the Mission. It includes Mission Dolores -- the oldest building in San Francisco, and Dolores Park -- one of the most popular parks in the city. As you may know, the Castro (centered 4 blocks west) is the historic gay center of San Francisco -- it features restaurants, bars, the Castro Theater, shopping, and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and day spas. The Mission (centered 3 blocks east) is a historically Latino neighborhood. It, too, features restaurants, bars, the Roxie Theater, shopping and an ever-increasing number of coffee shops and boutiques.

BART is also nearby -- the 16th & Mission station is only five blocks away. There is a bike share station 18th and Dolores street 3 blocks away. host_about:
20Mission - the neighborhood
Nestled in the culture rich Mission district, 20Mission is only a short walk from Dolores Park, Valencia Street's eccentric shopping, the best burritos you can get in the city, and an array of cultural landmarks.

20Mission - the feeling
Whether you're grabbing the first coffee of the day or the last snack of the night, you can always find someone familiar in the kitchen or common room. If you're busy working in your room you can still find out what's going on in our private slack conversations #Kitchen #Improvement #Activities, etc.

20Mission - the community
The people who live in 20Mission's 41 bedrooms share a kitchen, living room, and more than enough bathrooms/showers to go around. We also have common areas such as a rooftop and a courtyard, as well as coin-operated laundry machines. We host social events such as turning our entire floor into a life-sized monopoly board, chilling out with live music in the courtyard, and our notorious house parties.

20Mission - the people
Most people currently living at 20Mission are focused on entrepreneurship, tech, design and art. It's a great place to meet people who have more in-depth conversations and interactions. However, while we value creativity and innovation, we welcome people from all walks of life, regardless of their background. 

20Mission - moving in and prices. 
The monthly price of a small room is $1,700, a medium is $1,900 and a large is $2,100. 

This includes all utilities, fiber optic internet connection (the space has WiFi and each room also has a hard line connection), and an easy way to expand your social/professional network. We have a cleaning lady who cleans the kitchen, bathroom,and living room six days a week. If you think 20Mission and our current availability would work for you, please reply to this email to schedule a (Hidden by Airbnb) tour or on-site visit.

The best way to check us out is to schedule a visit!

The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture. It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. host_about:
It’s been said that knowing what someone is grateful for and the challenges they’ve overcome tells you a lot about them. For me there’s nothing in my life that I am more grateful for than my three adult sons who were also my life’s greatest challenge to raise as a single mother in San Francisco.  
In the crucible of parenthood, I have learned so much about working with people and developed qualities that are enormously beneficial in the world of work. When you have children whose lives depend on you, there’s no such thing as “I can’t” or “I’m tired” or “I couldn’t make it happen because…” Year in and year out, in life’s longest marathon, it became a deeply engrained habit to give my best every day and make it happen. 
 Being the sole responsible person for three growing boys required discipline, patience, diplomacy, negotiating skills, selflessness, tenacity, compassion, tenderness, endurance, resourcefulness, toughness and, last but not least, a thick skin. These same qualities are the foundation that has allowed me to succeed as an Executive Assistant for top executives at some stimulating and interesting companies, including early stage, privately held, and household-name corporations.  
Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place.

host_about:
Hello fellow travelers and hosts!

I am a BS in Business Administration at UC Berkeley, Walter A. Haas School of Business, a hotel concierge in San Francisco, and a to-be avid traveler. 

My living habits:
I'm highly adaptable, low maintenance, compliant, and incredibly understanding. Working in the Hotel Hospitality industry has taught me a few things about skewed perspectives on "the comfort of home." People live how they want to live, how they're familiar with living. 

When I'm traveling and staying in other homes, I strictly try to live as my hosts live, albeit with a keen sense of humility and circumspection. 

I'm fairly simple: I seek novelty where I can get it; I enjoy trying new things, seeing new places, and experiencing new sensations.  

I also have my hobbies and creature comforts: I enjoy a good game of tennis, a coffee, a book/my laptop, a warming fire, or even a beer or cocktail with a nice view and a good conversation with a friend, old or new (it's the connection that counts).

neighborhood_overview: Bernal Heights is a family-friendly neighborhood that blends the eclectic city-vibe of San Francisco with an intimate neighborhood setting that will make you feel like a local. It’s repeatedly ranked as one of the hottest S.F neighborhoods because of its warm climate, proximity to the city-center, neighborhood feel,  and of course the amazing Bay and City views from the top of Bernal Hill. Cortland Street is the is the commercial heart of the neighborhood, dotted with small locally-owned businesses that give Bernal a uniquely San Francisco feel. The apartment is half a block to Cortland, and about a 20 min downhill walk to the Mission district, with its world-famous restaurants and bars (the way back is uphill, so you may want go grab the bus or a Lyft!). With easy access to freeways and public transportation, Bernal Heights is a great place from which to explore the San Francisco Bay Area.

Bus Stops (67 and 24) are each a block or two away. BART is a 10 min 67 bus ride away or about a 20 min walk. Highways (101/280) are 3 mins away by car. Lyft, Uber, and Cabs are a very popular mode of transportation in San Franciso. Of course, if you're not afraid of the hills, walking is a great way to explore the City. PARKING: Street parking is free in the neighborhood (just make sure to check street cleaning times). Usually there are plenty of spaces on our street during the day, but the later it gets, it can sometimes be harder to find a space. Also, please be aware of San Francisco laws about parking on hills. You must turn your front wheels into the curb when parking downhill, and away from the curb when parking uphill. Otherwise you will be ticketed! Please don't block the driveway except for loading/unloading.

neighborhood_overview: The original site of the Ghirardelli Chocolate Factory (previously a woolen mill), are now the home of a stylish collection of shops and restaurants—one of the most pleasant places to stroll and shop in the city. Wind through passageways and across plazas to visit an assortment of boutiques and gift shops, or relax with bay views from a selection of restaurants. If you have kids along, you probably have one destination in mind more than any other: the Ghirardelli Soda Fountain and Chocolate Shop. The line can be out the door but don’t worry—it moves fast. name: Mini Modern Victorian in the Mission
summary: Welcome to our oasis in the Mission, SF's hippest, most diverse neighbourhood. We're a quick walk to the popular shops, restaurants and bars on Valencia, 20th and 24th Streets, or hop on the subway and zip up to bustling Union Square in minutes. If you need a break from the fun, relax on our deck with a glass of wine. This 850 sq ft Victorian was one of the first homes built in the city, and our recent renovation means you can stay in a bit of history while enjoying all the modern amenities.
space: One of three in a row, our one-floor house was one of the very first homes in the city, built around 1860 for the craftsmen who helped build many of the stunning Victorian mansions you'll see nearby. We renovated in March 2018, so all that historical character (11-foot ceilings, original Douglas Fir floors) is complimented by an open floor plan, brand new kitchen and bath,  laundry facilities, and a spot in our garage for your car. We've also installed a triple-glazed front window for peace and quiet at night so you can get some sleep after a long day of exploring the city.

neighborhood_overview: We could write a book about this place! Despite the rapid gentrification, the Mission is still a vibrant, authentic San Francisco neighbourhood, and our street is a microcosm of that. All walks of life meet on Shotwell, from the families who immigrated here in the 50s to the wealthy CEOs who've just moved in. Swarms of kids visit us on Halloween for our famous "Shotwell Stroll", but any time of year you'll see neighbours waving hello and chatting on the street. You'll also see the occasional homeless encampment pop up and there are still prostitutes who walk the streets at night. It's a mix that keeps things interesting and we wouldn't have it any other way. If you want to see the real San Francisco, you won't find a better spot.
transit: We are a 10-minute walk to the 24th Street BART station (which makes getting her from the airport quick and cheap). The #12 bus will pick you up a block away and drop you downtown in 25 minutes. Or just do what we do—walk! We're a 7-minute walk to the shops, restaurants and bars of Valencia, 20th and 24th Street. Stroll a little longer and you'll reach the lovely neighbourhoods of Hayes Valley, Lower Haight and Bernal Heights. And of course there's always Lyft and Uber to whisk you farther afield.
access: The house is yours. We live here, but our style is minimalist, modern and clutter-free so you'll feel like you're in your own SF pied-a-terre instead of someone else's home.
interaction: We won't be in the city during your stay, but you can always reach us quickly by text or phone, and almost as quickly by email. We'll also leave you lots of instructions, tips and recommendations to make your stay in our home as smooth and enjoyable as possible.
host_about: I'm a writer from Canada and my husband Hugo is an industrial designer from England. We met in New York and now we live in San Francisco (go figure). We love to travel and prefer to use Airbnb when we do, because it puts us in the heart of a real community (and we have a kitchen to make that vital first cup of tea in the morning). We've been on both sides of subletting so we know what it means to be a great guest. We are quiet, clean, respectful 40-somethings who will treat your home as well as our own. Happy travels!

I'm excited to start hosting and hope to live up to the hospitality I've experienced along the way.

neighborhood_overview: Depending on your mood, you can walk any direction from the apartment for a different taste of San Francisco. You are one block from Dolores Park in the Mission, which is a great spot to lounge on a sunny day. You can get a picnic from BiRite at 18th and Dolores (two blocks away). Mauerpark right at the corner of Church and 17th is a charming new bar/cafe worth dropping into. If you want to see what the Castro is all about, walk up 17th about three blocks towards the giant rainbow flag and the rest of the iconic neighborhood.  Mission Dolores church itself is also just a couple of blocks away at 16th and Dolores - a beautiful reminder of this neighborhood's history.  Plenty of cute bakeries around for breakfast. Le Marais bakery two blocks away at 17th and Sanchez is fun, or Tartine at 18th and Guerrero is very popular and delicious.
notes: No shoes inside please!
transit: Depending on where you're headed, you have various options as the apartment is very central to several Muni lines and BART. The J-Church Muni runs right on Church, about a block away. You can catch several other Muni lines at Church/Market, three blocks away. The 16th/Mission BART station is about a ten minute walk.

My goal as an Air BnB host is to make you feel at home and allow you to enjoy my lovely apartment and this amazing city while you're here. If you're visiting with children, I can give you lots of tips etc., just say the word!

The house is on a quiet block but walking distance (2.5 blocks) to Clement Street business district where there are a myriad of inexpensive restaurants and Asian markets. It is a truly unique corner of San Francisco where the flavor of "Old SF" still can be imbibed.
notes: Parking is not included and our car will be in the garage, but if you really think you need parking we will try to make that happen. The garden is shared with the guest in the garden apartment. host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was a member of the Armed Forces and was stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls and over to the Canadian side. 
Career wise, I’ve spent a decade working in property management and rentals. As a hobby, I write 90-minutes every morning at dawn, six-days a week. 
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. Nonetheless, if you desire an expansive view, relaxed comfort & accommodating ease of use (with reserved parking) this private room in a two bedroom flat is sublime. On a steep hill in residential Noe Valley (as opposed to downtown), it is so steep that walking 1/2 block to the bus stop is a genuine workout, so you may want a rental car or use Lyft/Uber. Naturally, people of all backgrounds are welcome. Only occasionally available. The very comfortable bedroom has a sliding glass door leading to a small deck and the floor plan provides for nice room-to-room privacy.  In addition to the shower, the bathtub is suitable for soaking.  The living room has a fireplace with gas starter and the view, well you can see the pictures. Morning sun fills the rooms.  The modest kitchen includes contemporary refrigerator, gas stove, dishwasher etc., along with a large raised breakfast table. Original to 1967, the bathroom and kitchen have ye
neighborhood_overview: House is in the upper (southern) Noe Valley neighborhood, bordering Glen Park and Diamond Heights neighborhoods. Noe Valley's exceptionally charming restaurant / commercial district on 24th Street is a hilly 20 minute walk north; 5 minutes by car. Notable Church Street restaurants are a hilly 10 minute walk away. Nearest grocery, pharmacy, bank, cleaners, post office are a hilly 10 minute walk away; 2 minutes by car.
notes: + Having a car here is very, very helpful: Even walking 1/2 block to the nearest bus stop can be very difficult because the sidewalks here are so steep. It is the price we pay for the great views living on a hillside provides. + Borders protected nature areas with a trail out of the back yard leading to extensive wooded hikes that even many lifelong San Franciscans do not know exist. + Hummingbirds are regular visitors, as are racoon, possum, skunk, coyote, hawk, owl, cedar waxwing...on and on. Last summer, a young cougar was captured one block away and, of course, was returned to a less threatening locale.  + Ridiculously plentiful parking, especially for San Francisco, including one spot in the driveway reserved for you.  + No broadcast or cable television, but you'll still be able to stream Portandia via the decent Wi-Fi, (20 down / 5 up).  + We can roll out the big screen monitor if you wish to watch DVDs or BluRays. + Pets allowed on a case by case basis. Please see house rules.
transit: A designated off-street parking space reserved for you.  Nearest bus stop is one steep uphill block away. Nearest MUNI light rail is two blocks downhill. access: Full access to the kitchen, ("well equipped," according to one guest), living/dining room, small deck and there is a spacious back yard with a gas grill and a view to the city.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. We love living here because it's a quiet place to retire to, while still being within walking distance of lots of restaurants, bars, parks, and everything else that SF has to offer. host_about:
I  have built my business—and my life—on harnessing the power of the self. Born and raised in the Midwest but a resident of San Francisco for the last fifteen years, my drive and passion for interior design propelled me to launch Gina Rachelle Design in 2012. Over the years, I have built an interior design studio that specializes in both residential and commercial spaces in this gorgeous city. // In 2016, my fiancé, Max, and I set out to remodel our own 1912 Edwardian home, Hermann Homestead. We designed the space to fit our lifestyle, and with a team of contractors we knocked out two walls and a closet creating an open floor plan and a larger bathroom. As an interior designer, it's always my goal to breathe life into a home with curated furnishings and details while never sacrificing function.

I loved coffee until I found out I was allergic to the coffee bean. Sweet or Savory? - Savory! Chip and Gauc are my last request if I were stuck on deserted island. Conversations are filled with life lessons, experiences and tips all with a bit of comedy. // My Top 5 favorite restaurants in San Francisco: 1. Cala, 2.Tacolicious, 3. Pizzeria Delfina, 4. Namu Gagi and 5. Statebird Provisions.

neighborhood_overview: The Potrero Hill district is one of the most unique neighborhoods in San Francisco and has gone through several changes from working class to the newer family oriented direction since the 1990's Potrero Hill is one of the sunniest neighborhoods in San Francisco.  It is insulated from our famous fog and chill from the ocean and gives some of the most spectacular views of downtown and the bay bridge.  If you are up for a few hills it can be a great walking experience and the ever growing "hub" of 18th street is always a great place to start a day. One of the best parts of Potrero Hill is that it is a neighborhood further from the "hustle and bustle" so it has a quiet and sleepy feel but you are never more than a few minutes from the fray.
notes: We just finished a renovation of our apartment this year and put a lot of our love into that work. Bus 10 (1 min walk) : The 10 bus picks you up just down the street at the corner of 20th and Arkansas.  It will take you through SOMA and into North Beach.  It eventually ends at Fort Mason  (Website hidden by Airbnb)  Bus 22 (5 min walk) : The 22 picks up at 18th and Connecticut just a few blocks away.  This bus will take you through the Mission, Haight/Ashbury, Fillmore and eventually ends at the Marina.  It also runs 24 hours a day!  (Website hidden by Airbnb)  Muni Train T (15 min walk): The T line is a great train found down 20th on 3rd in the Dogpatch district. neighborhood_overview: Though most visitors never make it past the restaurants and shops, Cole Valley does offer dramatic views of the city. The best spot is atop 600-foot-high Tank Hill (about 50 yards uphill from the house), named for an old water tank stationed there in the late 1800s. The eucalyptus trees there were planted after the attack on Pearl Harbor to hide the water tank from bombers. To get to the hill's summit and panoramic viewpoint, walk up Shrader Street to Belgrave Street and turn left, taking it to the end. Cole Valley may be one of the city's most interesting tourist destinations, while it makes for a relaxing respite from the Haight, and there are enough attractions for a day's outing. Food and coffee are the specialties in Cole Valley. In the three-block commercial strip along Cole Street and part of Carl Street, there are more than a dozen restaurants and caf?s, some of which draw visitors from around the Bay Area.

It’s been said that knowing what someone is grateful for and the challenges they’ve overcome tells you a lot about them. For me there’s nothing in my life that I am more grateful for than my three adult sons who were also my life’s greatest challenge to raise as a single mother in San Francisco.  
In the crucible of parenthood, I have learned so much about working with people and developed qualities that are enormously beneficial in the world of work. When you have children whose lives depend on you, there’s no such thing as “I can’t” or “I’m tired” or “I couldn’t make it happen because…” Year in and year out, in life’s longest marathon, it became a deeply engrained habit to give my best every day and make it happen. 
 Being the sole responsible person for three growing boys required discipline, patience, diplomacy, negotiating skills, selflessness, tenacity, compassion, tenderness, endurance, resourcefulness, toughness and, last but not least, a thick skin. These same qualities are the foundation that has allowed me to succeed as an Executive Assistant for top executives at some stimulating and interesting companies, including early stage, privately held, and household-name corporations.  
Perhaps the greatest blessing of all is good health and I’m grateful for that as well.  I’ve been told by so many people that I have more energy than anyone they’ve ever known that there must be some truth to it. In my entire life, I have very rarely been sick – even a common cold. It’s my belief this amazing gift of health and energy – of life – could be given to everyone in the world in equal measure to what I have received.  It’s my belief that this gift carries with it the responsibility to give my best to those I serve, and to make the world a better place.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality. host_about:
ABOUT ME

I grew up in Cleveland, Ohio and became an exchange student at the age of 16. Living abroad for one year in South Africa changed my life forever. I since went back to live in South Africa a second time. I have had the good fortune of traveling abroad and meeting amazing people along the way. I met a woman on a train who invited me to visit her in Paris. When I got there, she gave me the keys to her apartment and said I could stay as long as I like. From that moment on I made a vow to help as many travelers as possible on their journeys. That is why Air BNB appeals to me; the art of travel, connection, culture, and sharing the City I love so very much with others.

INTERESTS

Spiritual pursuits. Traditional Japanese culture. Tea. Gardening. Reading/listening to books. Taking care of my backyard wildlife. Exploring San Francisco. Cooking, when I have the time to enjoy it. I am passionate about Languages and learning. I am fluent in English, learning Spanish and Japanese, and previously studied Indo-Malay. I am enthusiastic about collecting words and phrases in other languages. I am passionate about animals and nature.

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS

I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R & B, Motown, Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.

Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.

I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,"The Glass Castle,"Your Brain at Work." I listen to Audio Books constantly which is why I get through so many books.

COUNTRIES I’VE VISITED

Japan, Peru, South Africa, Malaysia, Thailand, Switzerland, France, Belgium, Italy

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING

I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take a cruise. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general, I like to keep things simple. 

As a Host, however, I enjoy nurturing Guests and making sure they feel well cared for and even spoiled. My Guests enjoy my many versions of “tea” and also wicked bowls of popcorn! 

I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and desire to make even the ordinary feel special. 

From the lovely view, peaceful setting, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill requests, you can count on having a positive stay and look forward to a return visit to our beloved house on the hill in exciting San Francisco.

Renting our home is also funding a new apartment in the garage that will be for a long term tenant. Airbnb has also helped fund Wendy's food business 'Tartlet Bar': a farm direct sustainable food business between her families farm in Southern Oregon & San Francisco. 

Fred & Wendy own the house together, but split their time there with Lita their daughter. One of them will be there to meet you when you check in.

We have lived in San Francisco for nearly 30 years, but get out of the city as much as possible. 

Besides being a farmer, Wendy will always be an artist, writer, entrepreneur, designer and traveller. One of her passions is to see the world and study different cultures, which she has done extensively (she wants to be an anthropologist when she grows up ;.).  


We believe the world is Lita's education, with 3 languages and several countries already under her belt she is a gypsy at heart.

Fred is French, fluent in French, English & Spanish, a photographer, world traveler and owns two small business; Dalva (a bar in the mission district) and Grenouille-French Antiques in SF.

We're also doing Airbnb because we like the idea of meeting like minded travelers, people who seek adventure, people who believe we can learn from everyone we meet and enjoy absorbing other cultures as much as we (Website hidden by Airbnb) it possible to be part of a community while being a gypsy and a nomad? So far it's working out to be yes...

I trust that you will enjoy your stay immensely and will do my very best to make it ever so special and memorable. I'm completely dedicated to 5 star stays and welcome your feedback at any time.

Welcome! Come belong with us.
